title: 49ers to sign LB Quinton Bell
summary: Linebacker Quinton Bell will have a chance to make the 49ers' 53-man roster this summer.
full_text: '' Linebacker Quinton Bell will have a chance to make the 49ers' 53-man roster this summer. Bell worked out for the 49ers on Tuesday and Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the NFC West team will sign him after that tryout. Defensive end KJ Henry also landed a job during Tuesday's workout. Bell spent the last three seasons with the Dolphins. He appeared in 24 games and recorded 35 tackles, three tackles for loss, a sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during his time in Miami. Prior to joining the Dolphins, Bell appeared in games for the Falcons and Buccaneers. He had three tackles in nine appearances for those clubs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Matthew Stafford: We have a high ceiling, have to continue raising our floor
summary: The Rams were among the favorites for Super Bowl LXI before they traded for Myles Garrett in June and acquiring the defensive player of the year has only pushed expectations for the coming season higher in Los Angeles.
full_text: The Rams were among the favorites for Super Bowl LXI before they traded for Myles Garrett in June and acquiring the defensive player of the year has only pushed expectations for the coming season higher in Los Angeles. Head coach Sean McVay acknowledged those expectations at the start of training camp while noting that " there’s a lot of stuff in the midst of the journey that we don’t control." McVay wants the Rams to prioritize the things they do control when it comes to preparing for the season and quarterback Matthew Stafford was in a similar frame of mind when he spoke to reporters on Monday. Stafford said he wants the team to focus on improving their baseline level of play rather than thinking about how high they can climb if everything falls into place. “We can’t help but make each other better, [but] pieces of paper and names on a roster, those don’t win football games,” Stafford said, via Greg Beacham of the Associated Press. “Teams and players and groups do. . . . Sean said it the other night, we’ve got potentially a high ceiling, right? We’ve got great players that have done a lot in this league. What can we do to continue to raise our floor , so if I’m off a little bit, we can still go find a way to win a football game? If our defense is off a little bit, we can still find a way to go win a football game. Continuing to raise that floor is something that’s going to be a huge part of our journey this season.” There are a number of ways that a talented team can get thrown off track over the course of an NFL season. The work that Stafford and the Rams do now can't eliminate all of them, but anything they can do to pare that number down will help them weather the inevitable curveballs that come their way over the next few months.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mickey Loomis: Hopeful about Chris Olave contract extension, but not there yet
summary: Wide receiver Chris Olave's contract was a topic of conversation at Saints General Manager Mickey Loomis's press conference on Tuesday.
full_text: Wide receiver Chris Olave's contract was a topic of conversation at Saints General Manager Mickey Loomis's press conference on Tuesday. Olave is in the final year of his rookie deal after posting career highs across the board during the 2025 season and Loomis said that the team is working to sign him to an extension in the near future. "We're having a lot of discussions ," Loomis said. "You have meetings and we're just not there yet. We're hopeful. . . . We want to get it done. Chris and his agents, I know they want to get it done. But it’s got to be right for both parties." Olave was limited this offseason after missing the final game of last season with a blood clot in his lung. He's also dealt with multiple concussions and Loomis called his injury history "an element" to the conversations about his next contract, but he's ready for a full workload this summer and the health issues haven't dimmed the Saints' desire to keep Olave in their offense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Leonard Williams: There's been a few conversations about a new contract
summary: Jalen Carter agreed to a new deal with the Eagles this week that will make him the highest-paid defensive tackle in the league and that development is of interest to plenty of people outside of Philadelphia.
full_text: ' Jalen Carter agreed to a new deal with the Eagles this week that will make him the highest-paid defensive tackle in the league and that development is of interest to plenty of people outside of Philadelphia. One interested party could be found in Seattle. Seahawks defensive tackle Leonard Williams is heading into the final year of his current deal, which has an average annual salary of $21.5 million. That ranks 14th at the position for a player who was a second-team All-Pro last season. Williams might not jump back to the top of the heap at this point in his career, but he said Tuesday that he's had "a few conversations" with the team about extending his stay in Seattle. Williams said he's doing his best to keep those conversations from impacting his preparation for the season. "I try not to think about it , honestly," Williams said, via Brady Henderson of ESPN.com. "I've always been that type of guy. I've obviously had a lot of contracts at this point in my career, and I've always noticed players that really focus on their contract end up not playing well, they end up having their head in the wrong place, and I've noticed that when I focus on just being where I'm at, focusing on my team and how I can get better individually, things always tend to work themselves out." The Seahawks are also talking contract with cornerback Devon Witherspoon, so there could be multiple contract announcements in the near future if all goes well for two of their top defensive players.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ben Johnson: Caleb Williams has it all, there's nothing he can't do
summary: "Elite arm talent, playmaking ability, escape-ability. He has his legs that he can hurt a defense with. There's just so many layers to who he is as a player," Johnson said of Williams.
full_text: Bears head coach Ben Johnson says he has a uniquely talented quarterback in Caleb Williams. "He's got it all," Johnson said of Williams. "There's really nothing he can't do. Elite arm talent, playmaking ability, escape-ability. He has his legs that he can hurt a defense with. There's just so many layers to who he is as a player. That word 'consistency' comes up over the course of a 60-minute game — or more if we need it — where we're getting high-level quarterback play throughout that game. You see flashes of it, and we're trying to tap into that, where we're just consistently delivering the ball where it needs to go, giving it to our guys, and then we all know that he has that ability to put on that Superman cape when the time calls for it." Johnson did acknowledge that he needs to see improvement in Williams' completion percentage. Last year Williams completed just 58.1 percent of his passes, which ranked dead last among the 32 quarterbacks who threw at least 250 passes in 2025. This year Johnson wants to see Williams complete 70 percent of his passes. "He's done a great job over the spring and summer, just looking at himself, body position-wise, from an accuracy standpoint, are my feet aligned to where I want to throw the ball?" Johnson said. "The ability to see where I should go with the football, to process a little faster, that's where I'm hopeful that we see another step in terms of the processing speed." A 70 percent completion rate, which only one quarterback in the NFL (Drake Maye) achieved last season, may be an unrealistic expectation for Williams. But Johnson believes Williams is capable of doing just about anything at the quarterback position.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Michael Strahan responds to criticism over Chris Johnson interview
summary: Strahan defends not mentioning the link between ALS and football.
full_text: ' Hall of Fame defensive end and multi-platform TV personality Michael Strahan took some criticism last month for not mentioning the connection between ALS and football in his interview with former NFL running back Chris Johnson, who disclosed that he has the disease. Appearing on Tuesday's edition of The Dan Patrick Show , Patrick asked Strahan if, in retrospect, Strahan believes he should have asked that question. “Well, I had that — I actually thought about that , because I saw what every[one said], ‘Well you should have asked this, you should have asked that.’ Well, you should have got the interview. How about that?” Strahan said. “That’s one thing." That's one sort of petty thing. The "get" doesn't become a license to not get to the right questions. It also invites the question, generally speaking, as to whether an "exclusive" interview was less of a "get" and more of a "give" to someone who won't ask the most probing and necessary questions. “Two," Strahan told Patrick, "two, that was Chris’s moment for Chris to share the story which Chris wanted to share. And when I got the call that Chris wanted to share that he has, you know, ALS, that was the story. It wasn’t for me to try to grandstand, which — I hate when people do this, Dan. As an interviewer, our job is [to] deliver information. I’m not trying to get a bigger name for myself by putting somebody else in an uncomfortable position. I was there as a service to Chris, for what Chris wanted people to understand and know about his life and where he was now. I was not there to make a story about myself or to get a big headline — that’s what it wasn’t about. The headlines were about Chris is where they needed to be. "I did ask Chris about football, how the NFL has been supportive and all those things. He has twin boys who play football right now. So there are so many things that people don't know but a few were critical of, but overall I'm very proud of what we did there at ABC in bringing that story. And I'm very proud and very happy that Chris trusted us to tell it. Because that was Chris's story to tell. The headline's about Chris Johnson, not about Michael Strahan. I don't make any of these things about myself. And that was the disappointing thing for a few people who were critical of that. But if you don't have critics that means you're not doing a good job, too.” Many would say that's not how an interview should work, even on a feel-good network morning show. Certain topics are unavoidable. It's not "grandstanding" to ask an obvious question and to trust that the subject of the interview will be able to handle it. "Do you believe your ALS is a result of playing football?" If yes, "Would you have still played football if you knew then what you know now?" (The fact that Johnson's sons play football makes those questions even more appropriate.) And it's obvious that there's a connection between ALS and football, starting with the fact that ALS is a no-questions-asked condition that triggers payment under the NFL's concussion settlement fund and continuing with the studies that show an increased risk of ALS for those who played in the NFL. Here's the other point that Strahan didn't address. After the interview, when Strahan and his colleagues discussed the situation in the studio, the obvious connection could have, and arguably should have, been mentioned. Indeed, Strahan's narration of the interview included the conclusion that Johnson's diagnosis was attributed not to a family history of ALS but to the 90 percent of ALS cases that are regarded as "sporadic" with no known cause. As noted by Brendon Kleen of Awful Announcing , the separate online story from ABC also failed to address the clear link between ALS and football. And so, even if Strahan is disappointed by the criticism, the criticism is fair. Even if he didn't feel comfortable in asking Johnson about the connection between ALS and football (Strahan didn't mention to Patrick whether Johnson asked before the interview to avoid that topic), ABC could have — and absolutely should have — addressed it. Failing to do so invites questions as to whether ABC tiptoed around the established link between ALS and football as a favor to the NFL, which now owns 10 percent of ABC's sister company, ESPN, especially since Strahan's defense to the criticism included a comment that he asked Johnson "how the NFL has been supportive" of him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Plaxico Burress: Playing for the Jets and going to prison were "kind of similar"
summary: Plaxico Burress's NFL career was put on hold during the 2008 season, when he accidentally shot himself and then went to prison for 20 months for carrying a gun illegally.
full_text: Plaxico Burress's NFL career was put on hold during the 2008 season, when he accidentally shot himself and then went to prison for 20 months for carrying a gun illegally. When he got out of prison in 2011, he signed with the Jets. Burress now says the two experiences were a lot alike. At the time of the infamous shooting, Burress and the Giants were 10-1 and the favorites to repeat as Super Bowl champions, and Burress was just months into a new five-year, $35 million contract. The shooting ended Burress's tenure with the Giants, whose season went into a tailspin afterward, and when Burress returned to the NFL he signed a one-year, $3 million contract with a mediocre Jets team. “They’re both kind of similar because when I walked into prison my first day, I was like, ‘Damn, man, you are a fucking loser,” Burress said on The Joint Venture Show . “And I had the same damn feeling every day I walked through the door with the Jets. I was like, ‘Damn I hope we can win this weekend.’ Loser.” Burress caught 45 passes for 612 yards and eight touchdowns for the 2011 Jets, who went 8-8 and missed the playoffs. He then played briefly for the Steelers in 2012, and his career ended with a training camp injury in Pittsburgh in 2013.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Leonard Williams, Cooper Kupp make case for grass fields
summary: The NFLPA's P.R. push for grass fields should focus less on making a broad-brush effort to shame the owners into choosing a better surface and more on getting specific teams to flip.
full_text: ' The NFLPA's P.R. push for grass fields should focus less on making a broad-brush effort to shame the owners into choosing a better surface and more on getting specific teams to flip. That effort, as previously explained, should start with the Seahawks , who are in the process of getting a new owner. On Tuesday, a pair of Seattle veterans made the case for grass during training-camp press conferences. Defensive lineman Leonard Williams was asked whether seeing temporary grass at Lumen Field for the World Cup made him wish the grass would remain permanently. "For sure," Williams told reporters, "I think the whole NFL felt that way. We obviously prefer to be on grass. It's less impact, better on the body. I understand there’s a lot of things that go into having grass in the stadium that I don’t fully understand yet, but if it was up to a player and it just came down to grass or turf, we obviously prefer grass." Receiver Cooper Kupp was initially more concise. “That would be sweet," he said with a laugh. Why the laugh? “It would be awesome," Kupp said. "I've been vocal about it in the past. There's so many moving parts, which I get. What we need to do -- there’s a great crew that works out in that shed out there. It's a great crew that keeps this [practice field] grass nice. Go ask them, ‘Hey, what would it look like?’ I don't know the ‘grassology’ of all that stuff. You got soccer teams playing on it, you have a lot of stuff happening. You have events being hosted. I would like to think with all the resources in the NFL that we can make that happen. There's people that can make that happen. We need to, as players, keep voicing what we want and what we think is important, but eventually I do think it'll get done.” The best place to start would be in Seattle. “It makes a huge difference," Kupp said regarding the difference between grass and artificial turf. "I know all the metrics and all the data that say the injury rates of this, but I don't know. I know how I feel. You ask a lot of players who will say the same thing. Whether injury rates change or not, I know how my body feels, everything on turf versus grass. You can ask coaches how their backs feel after standing on the turf versus grass. Coaches have a lot of other issues. But it does make a difference. . . . "It's possible. I know it's possible. It's a conversation that needs to continue.” At some point, the conversation needs to become action. It has become a Collective Bargaining Agreement issue, which means that the players will have to give something up in order to get grass on all fields. But the individual teams can still choose grass over turf, like the Bills have done in their new stadium. With the Seahawks soon having a new owner, why not launch a concerted effort to get Vinod Khosla to install a high-quality grass field that can be properly maintained and protected during the other events held at Lumen Field? Talk is cheap. Grass fields aren't. The players need to find a way to get more owners to ignore misleading injury data and to focus on the overwhelming anecdotal evidence that the players who have to perform on grass or turf strongly prefer grass because of how their bodies feel after playing on it, versus how they feel after playing on a surface that causes the extreme forces they create to ricochet back into their ankles, knees, and hips.
author: Mike Florio

title: Geno Smith "hates" the fact that he created a potential "distraction" for Jets
summary: Smith was happy to put recent domestic dispute behind him.
full_text: Quarterback Geno Smith is back with the Jets. In the first offseason of his second tenure with the team, Smith was involved in an incident that sparked an on-again, off-again police investigation. (The probe is currently off.) On Tuesday, in his first press conference since the situation unfolded, Smith expressed regret for creating an off-field issue for his team. "I really hate the fact that something I was a part of c ould’ve been a distraction for this team , my teammates and this organization because a lot of hard work has been put in," Smith said, via Rich Cimini of ESPN. "A lot of guys have put in a lot of work for us to be in a good spot as a team. I'm happy that I'm able to put this behind me. I'm looking forward to moving forward." Smith, per Cimini, also said he discussed the situation with coach Aaron Glenn, General Manager Darren Mougey, and veteran leaders on the team. Smith did not elaborate on what was said. And while the investigation currently has been closed, it could still open again — if, for example, the alleged victim decides to provide police with a sworn statement. The full police report suggested that there were multiple skirmishes between Smith and his accuser. Smith also claimed that she had tried to steal $20 million in watches and jewelry during the dispute.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saquon Barkley wants to be remembered for more than backward hurdle
summary: Saquon Barkley's backward hurdle from 2024 immediately became one of the best plays in NFL history.
full_text: ' Saquon Barkley's backward hurdle from 2024 immediately became one of the best plays in NFL history. The too-good-to-be-true move even made its way onto Madden 25. As good as it was, Barkley doesn't want to be known for it. “When I got to the locker room and got to see the play, I realized I was able to do something pretty cool ,” Barkley told Chris Bumbaca of USA Today. “It’s something. It’s a play I’ll never forget. But I also don’t want to be remembered for that play. “I’m happy I was able to make that play, but I’m ready for the next one.” Odell Beckham never did anything better than his one-handed catch for a touchdown over Cowboys cornerback Brandon Carr in 2014. The wide receiver once said, "It's unfortunate, in a way, to be known only for the catch." Barkley has had a 2,000-yard season, won Offensive Player of the Year and won a Super Bowl ring, all in the same season. But he had only 1,140 yards last season, and the Eagles went 11-6 and lost in the wild-card round. Barkley wants more than last season. “So that’s a motivation for me -- try to get back to that game,” Barkley said. “That’s why I train the way I train. I would love to have had a faster start last year, but you can’t get caught up in the stats. You can’t get too caught up in numbers. Some of my better years weren’t based off numbers. It was based off how I handled myself in certain situations.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Bodycam video of Tony Romo arrest is released
summary: The video from the arrest of former Cowboys quarterback and CBS analyst Tony Romo has emerged.
full_text: '' The video from the arrest of former Cowboys quarterback and CBS analyst Tony Romo has emerged. TMZ has obtained and published bodycam video and audio from both his initial traffic stop and his field sobriety test. The first video shows his initial traffic stop. After Romo is told that he needs to submit to a field sobriety test, Romo repeatedly asks if he can call his lawyer. The deputy repeatedly tells Romo he can't. He then appears to proceed with the call. When the deputy calls for further assistance, he agrees to comply. Because he was pulled over on a busy highway (and a bridge), the officer explains that she'll be taking him to a level area for the test. In the second video, Romo conducts the test in bare feet. He seems to not understand the instructions for a fairly simple heel-to-toe walking exercise. "Do you understand the instructions?" he's asked. "No," Romo says. "I don't. There's too many." He also explains that he has had "two back surgeries" before engaging in the heel-to-toe walking test. With each step, his heel lands far in front of his toe. Romo then is asked to stand on one leg. Initially, he can't decide which leg to use. After he picks his left leg, Romo uses his arms to help balance himself. After the deputy stops the test, Romo is asked if he'll submit to breath testing. "We're not doing that," Romo says. "I hear from all the lawyers, 'Don't ever do that.' So we're not gonna do that." Romo then asks, "Did I pass this test?" "Turn around," the deputy replies. "No, I didn't. Huh?" As the arrest process begins, Romo asks if he can make a call because "there's a plane taking off." He is then told he's under arrest.
author: Mike Florio

title: Adam Peters gets a creative question about Brandon Aiyuk
summary: When it comes to players under contract with one team, other teams generally shy away from saying anything about him.
full_text: When it comes to players under contract with one team, other teams generally shy away from saying anything about him. To comment on the player is to risk a tampering jackpot. On Tuesday, JP Finlay of NBC 4 in D.C. came up with a way to ask about 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk, without asking about 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk. Finlay asked Commanders G.M. Adam Peters "in a general sense" whether a potential player's social-media habits is a factor in the analysis as to whether he should be added to the roster. " That’s a good roundabout question ," Peters said. "We look at everything, JP. I mean, it's a great question, but we do look at everything and, you know, we want to make sure it's the right player to be in our locker room and our bloodstream and in our culture and, you know, we often, you know, we look at that stuff. I mean, it's not always the first thing we look at. Obviously, you're looking at the tape, and you talk to the teams that the players have been on, and how they were in the locker room, the players have played with them, and so on and so forth to make those decisions. But, you know, that's not usually a huge part of it. Usually." Commanders coach Dan Quinn, who called Finlay a "straight badass" before Peters answered, added this after Peters answered: "Well played. Both of you." And so, yes, Aiyuk's recent social-media adventures (or misadventures, as the case may be) will play a role in whether the Commanders sign him. Another factor, obviously, will be whether quarterback Jayden Daniels is jostling to add Aiyuk. None of it matters until Aiyuk applies to the league office for reinstatement from the 49ers' reserve/left squad list to the 90-man roster. But if Aiyuk ever does what he needs to do to set the stage for his release, the Commanders may be interested — but the social-media stuff will indeed be considered.
author: Mike Florio

title: Notre Dame gets an even better jersey patch deal than Ohio State
summary: There's gold in them thar jerseys.
full_text: There's gold in them thar jerseys. Literally. On the same day Ohio State landed a deal with JPMorgan Chase at reportedly north of $15 million per year , Notre Dame reportedly has a deal with SoFi, via Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports, at an average of $18 million to $20 million per year . It's the latest effort to turn college football jerseys into billboards, with programs that need to generate more money looking for ways to do so. And the presence of jersey patches on college football uniforms will lead to even more. Which eventually will result in the NFL following suit in the effort to put ads on their in-game fits. It's coming. Like it or not. Actually, it's amazing it hasn't happened yet. It's found money for the NFL. Every year it doesn't happen, it's money lost. When will it happen? Who knows? But it's something the NFL Players Association should pushing for it. The revenue is shared. Why not maximize it?
author: Mike Florio

title: Bucs announce three roster moves
summary: The Buccaneers announced three roster moves on Tuesday, the day before their first 2026 training camp practice.
full_text: The Buccaneers announced three roster moves on Tuesday, the day before their first 2026 training camp practice. The team waived rookie safety Ja'Qurious Conley with a non-football injury designation. They also placed cornerback Chase Lucas and defensive lineman Haggai Ndubuisi on the active/physically unable to perform list. Players can be removed from the PUP list after passing a physical. Conley signed with the Buccaneers as an undrafted free agent out of Charlotte. He played three seasons at North Carolina before transferring to Charlotte in 2024, and in 2025, he registered 64 tackles and three interceptions. Lucas entered the NFL as a seventh-round pick of the Lions in 2022. He made Detroit's roster as a rookie and played 18 games in two seasons there, contributing six tackles. During the 2024 offseason, he signed with the 49ers and ended up on the practice squad for the entire campaign. Lucas then made San Francisco's active roster in 2025. In his 15 games played last season, Lucas totaled nine tackles, a pass defensed and a quarterback hit. Ndubuisi first participated in the International Player Pathway Program in 2022 and was allocated to the Cardinals as an offensive tackle. He saw action in one preseason game before being released by the Cardinals. The following season, he returned to the NFL through the IPPP, this time going to the Broncos as a defensive lineman. He spent the 2023 campaign on Denver's practice squad, then signed with Washington in 2024 and landed on the Commanders' practice squad for the balance of that season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chargers sign LS Peter Bowden
summary: The Chargers made the release of offensive guard Ben Cleveland official on Tuesday.
full_text: The Chargers made the release of offensive guard Ben Cleveland official on Tuesday. They signed long snapper Peter Bowden in a corresponding move. Bowden returns to the Chargers after spending the end of the 2025 season on the team’s practice squad. He entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2024 with Green Bay, spending training camp with the Packers. Later that season, Bowden joined the Jaguars' practice squad. Bowden snapped collegiately at Wisconsin, appearing in 39 career games from 2021-23. He was a finalist for the Patrick Mannelly Award in 2023, which recognizes college football’s top long snapper. That season, Bowden snapped on an operation that helped Badgers kicker Nathanial Vakos earn All-Big Ten recognition.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jerry Jones is willing to give up a top pick for a defensive playmaker
summary: The Cowboys owner said he talked to another owner about a trade as recently as Monday.
full_text: '' The Cowboys believe they have a team ready to compete for a Super Bowl championship, but that doesn't mean they are satisfied with their roster. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he has had trade discussions with another owner as recently as Monday, calling it a "very legitimate discussion." "I'd be very interested," Jones said Tuesday during the team's annual news conference to open training camp. "I'd give up the future to [get something] substantive to where we are today — as to a player — to give you an idea about what I invest, something substantive, to get the right kind of deal and improve us for opening day. I would. I feel that good about this team this year. Of course, you know that I haven't seen this team play together, but in general, looking ahead, I think we've got a chance to be worthy of spending some future if we saw an opportunity." Jones elaborated to reporters after the news conference, saying the Cowboys still could use a playmaker on defense, like a pass rusher or a linebacker. The team, of course, traded one of the league's top pass rushers, Micah Parsons, to the Packers before the start of last season. “If we get an opportunity to add to this thing, we’re very capable of doing that ,” Jones said, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. “The mood is here to do it. . . . If any place it would be to improve our play-making ability on defense and pressure that quarterback or have an opportunity to do something special at linebacker. A top pick is expendable this year to add somebody meaningful that would help us now. I’m not just looking for a player; we’re looking for somebody that can add to the mix.” The Cowboys seem to believe they are one player away from a sure-fire Super Bowl team, a feeling they haven't felt in years despite Jones' annual optimism. Jones didn't win his first Super Bowl until the Cowboys traded for pass rusher Charles Haley just before the start of the 1992 season. He didn't win his third until the Cowboys signed cornerback Deion Sanders from the 49ers after losing to San Francisco in the 1994 NFC Championship Game. At some point, for some reason, Jones stopped being the riverboat gambler. That's why it's been more than 30 years since the Cowboys' last championship, which Dak Prescott reminded everyone of Monday when he showed up to training camp in a Super Bowl XXX championship T-shirt . "I may have been trying to get a little of both in — a little for today, but also save a little for tomorrow," Jones said. "But then, you end up with a little milk toast sometimes. When that happens for you, you need to be a little more definitive. I will domino. I will lay it out there. It's not a threat. It's just that I will shoot. So, yeah, we're very capable, if we get the opportunity to improve it by doing it. My message simply is that I feel good enough about this thing to give up some of the future, if the opportunity comes up."
author: Charean Williams

title: Commanders offensive assistant Wes Welker will work with the team's tight ends
summary: The Commanders will stay in house to replace tight ends coach Ben Steele.
full_text: The Commanders will stay in house to replace tight ends coach Ben Steele. Head coach Dan Quinn said that offensive assistant Wes Welker will now work with that position group. Steele was dismissed on Monday for violating team rules. Welker also worked with the team's tight ends at the end of their offseason program. Steele was placed on paid leave after a DWI arrest on June 7. Welker was a personnel analyst for the Commanders last season. The longtime NFL wideout was previously a wide receivers coach for the Dolphins and 49ers. He also spent time on the Texans' coaching staff after retiring as a player.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders sign P Matt Haack with Tress Way sidelined by pec injury
summary: Commanders punter Tress Way isn't healthy enough to practice with the team right now, so they have brought in another veteran to handle the duties at training camp.
full_text: '' Commanders punter Tress Way isn't healthy enough to practice with the team right now, so they have brought in another veteran to handle the duties at training camp. The agents for Matt Haack announced that their client is signing with the team after a workout on Tuesday. Haack appeared in seven games for the Cardinals last season and has also played for the Dolphins, Bills, Colts, Browns and Giants. Commanders General Manager Adam Peters said that Way is dealing with a pectoral injury. The three-time Pro Bowler is not expected to be out for an extended period of time. Peters also said that linebacker Kain Medrano will miss time with a hamstring injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants sign DL Marlon Davidson
summary: The Giants had a big group of players in for workouts ahead of the start of training camp and they announced the signing of two of them on Tuesday.
full_text: The Giants had a big group of players in for workouts ahead of the start of training camp and they announced the signing of two of them on Tuesday. Defensive tackle Marlon Davidson and tight end Tyler Moore are the newest additions to the 90-man roster. The team did not need to make any corresponding moves after waiving linebacker Cam Jones and defensive lineman C.J. Ravenell over the weekend. Davidson played one game for the Texans last season and five games for the Titans in 2023. He opened his career by appearing in 19 games for the Falcons after being drafted in the second round in 2020. Davidson has 40 tackles, two sacks, an interception, and a fumble recovery over his 25 appearances. The NFL's daily transaction reports shows that Giants tight end Thomas Fidone and defensive tackle Sam Roberts have been activated after passing their physicals.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rams' Justin Dedich out with “a hand accident around the Fourth of July," Sean McVay says
summary: When the Rams announced that guard Justin Dedich would open training camp on the non-football injury list, they did not reveal the nature of that injury.
full_text: ' When the Rams announced that guard Justin Dedich would open training camp on the non-football injury list , they did not reveal the nature of that injury. Today they explained it. Rams head coach Sean McVay said Justin Dedich “had a hand accident around the Fourth of July, and so that's kind of what's keeping him out for now.” McVay didn't specifically mention fireworks, but that's the obvious conclusion people will draw from a July 4 hand accident. During Fourth of July weekend in 2015, two different NFL players lost fingers in fireworks accidents. Giants defensive end Jason Pierre-Paul's injury caused him to miss half that season, although he had a long career after that, including being a Pro Bowler and Super Bowl champion in Tampa Bay in 2020. Buccaneers cornerback C.J. Wilson also suffered a serious hand injury at Fourth of July 2015 and never played again. There's been no word on the severity of Dedich's injury. Dedich signed with the Rams as an undrafted rookie out of USC in 2024 and has played in 29 games for them, with nine starts. UPDATE: Dedich’s injury was reportedly not fireworks-related, and he is expected to return soon .
author: Michael David Smith

title: Denzel Ward agrees to two-year contract extension with Browns
summary: Ward's agents told reporters that it's a $62.2 million deal with $52.3 million guaranteed.
full_text: Browns cornerback Denzel Ward made it clear this offseason that he wanted to stay in Cleveland . Now he and the Browns have agreed to a deal to make that happen. Ward and the Browns have agreed to a two-year contract extension. Ward's agents told reporters that it's a $62.2 million deal with $52.3 million guaranteed and makes Ward the highest-paid defensive back in the NFL. The 29-year-old Ward is an Ohio native who was drafted by the Browns with the fourth overall pick in 2018 after starring at Ohio State. He has been one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL and now appears set to play out his prime years in Cleveland. With the Browns in the midst of a rebuild, they could have considered trading Ward, just as they traded Myles Garrett. But while Garrett wanted out, Ward did not. So Ward remains in Cleveland, and will get paid a lot to do so.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mason Rudolph to begin camp as Steelers' No. 2 QB
summary: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy generally has carried only three quarterbacks during training camp.
full_text: '' Steelers coach Mike McCarthy generally has carried only three quarterbacks during training camp. He has four in his first season in Pittsburgh. It's a unique situation with starter Aaron Rodgers in his final season, and the Steelers evaluating their future at the position. Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar are behind Rodgers, and the Steelers could keep all four into the season. "I don’t know why it wouldn’t be [an option],” coach Mike McCarthy said Tuesday, via Chris Adamski of triblive.com. “I’m not philosophically opposed to keeping the best players.” Rudolph, the nine-year veteran, will start training camp as the No. 2. That is a change from the offseason when Howard received the second-team reps. “Aaron will take the ‘ones;’ Mason will start out with the second group; and Will and Drew will take the third-group reps,” McCarthy said. “That’s the way we’ll start.” Allar is a third-round pick who could be the heir apparent. But the Steelers will have to figure out how to get him enough reps for him to be ready to compete in 2027, while getting Rodgers ready to start his final season and Rudolph or Howard ready to back up Rodgers. “The responsibility to get the starter ready is not only on the quarterback coach and the play caller, but it’s also on the other quarterbacks,” McCarthy said. “And then the starter’s responsibility is to make sure those other three are connected. We’ve got to move the room along.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Justin Dedich will return soon, Fourth of July injury was not fireworks-related
summary: When Rams head coach Sean McVay said today that guard Justin Dedich was out of training camp because he “had a hand accident around the Fourth of July," it was reasonable to infer that McVay was describing a fireworks accident.
full_text: When Rams head coach Sean McVay said today that guard Justin Dedich was out of training camp because he “ had a hand accident around the Fourth of July ," it was reasonable to infer that McVay was describing a fireworks accident. But apparently not. Mike Garafolo reports that Dedich's injury was not a fireworks accident, Dedich did not lose any fingers, and he will be back to playing in the near future. That's much better news than was suggested by McVay's description, which invoked memories of July 4, 2015, when two different NFL players lost fingers in fireworks accidents. Giants defensive end Jason Pierre-Paul missed half of that season, while Buccaneers cornerback C.J. Wilson's fireworks injury was career-ending. Fortunately, Dedich's injury does not appear to be of that nature, and the Rams can expect him back on the field soon.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tank Dell avoids PUP list to open Texans camp
summary: Wide receiver Tank Dell said in June that he felt he'd be ready to go at the start of training camp and it appears the Texans agree with his assessment of his health.
full_text: Wide receiver Tank Dell said in June that he felt he'd be ready to go at the start of training camp and it appears the Texans agree with his assessment of his health. Dell was not one of the players that the team placed on their physically unable to perform list on Tuesday. Dell missed all of last season after suffering a severe knee injury in December 2024 and was able to do limited work during the team's offseason program. Dell had 98 catches for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns in his first two NFL seasons. Linebacker E.J. Speed and safety M.J. Stewart have been placed on the PUP list. Speed tore his quad this offseason and could miss the entire season. The Texans also placed wide receiver Jaylin Noel on the non-football injury list.
author: Josh Alper

title: Packers put Micah Parsons on PUP list
summary: Micah Parsons was not part of the initial batch of Packers players to land on the teams physically unable to perform list, but word was that the move was coming on Tuesday and it is now official.
full_text: Micah Parsons was not part of the initial batch of Packers players to land on the teams physically unable to perform list, but word was that the move was coming on Tuesday and it is now official. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that the defensive end has been moved to the list along with offensive tackle Brant Banks, long snapper Matt Orzech, defensive end Jordon Riley, and defensive tackle Nazir Stackhouse. The Packers also signed kicker Lenny Krieg and tight end Thomas Yassmin. Defensive tackle Dante Barnett and kicker Lucas Havrisik were waived to round out the day's moves. Parsons is not expected to be ready to return from his torn ACL until October at the earliest. He can move to the reserve version of the PUP list at the cut to 53 players, which would keep him out at least four games. The Packers placed six other players on injury lists Monday and all of the players can be activated at any point during training camp.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers to sign DE KJ Henry
summary: The 49ers are making an addition to their defensive line group.
full_text: '' The 49ers are making an addition to their defensive line group. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that they will sign defensive end KJ Henry. Henry worked out for the team on Tuesday, Henry was a Commanders fifth-round pick in 2023 and he was let go as part of their final cuts in 2024. He was claimed by the Bengals and later moved on to the Cowboys and Eagles before the year was out. Henry also spent time with the Browns and Steelers last season. Henry appeared in 15 games across all of those spots. He has 22 tackles and 2.5 sacks for his career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Kyle Shanahan was holding, using cell phone at time of accident
summary: Shanahan was not cited for violation of California Vehicle Code.
full_text: '' The 49ers' successful effort to keep the Kyle Shanahan car accident under wraps until the day the team reported to training camp served only to make people wonder why it was so important to treat the situation with extreme secrecy. Which has caused some to wonder whether there's more to the story. Here's something more to the story, as found by Grant Cohn of SI.com. Citing and linking to a public, governmental website, Cohn reports that Shanahan was holding and using a cellphone at the time of the accident. Via Cohn, the website indicates that Shanahan was in violation of California Vehicle Code 23123.5(a) , which prohibits holding and operating a cell phone while driving. Shanahan was not cited, however. The other driver, per Cohn, was deemed to be at fault because she swerved into Shanahan's lane and caused a head-on collision. Airbags in both cars were deployed. The initial ESPN report, posted minutes after the 49ers presumably authorized the release of the information, indicates that the other driver suffered no injuries . Shanahan, in contrast, sustained a broken nose, a broken hand, broken ribs, and a severe concussion. He also needed 40 stitches to close the lacerations in his face. (On Monday's PFT Live , Chris Simms said Shanahan nearly lost his right eye .) The fact that Cohn was able to find this information underscores the reality that the local media, consciously or not, ignored the story until it was reported. Most news organizations have employees who actively monitor all public reports and databases for incidents involving public figures. Either the reporters whose media outlets cover the 49ers weren't looking for the information or they found it but opted to say nothing or the information was withheld and/or slow-played by the public agencies. Even now, it doesn't seem that the entities who actively track all things 49ers are exploring the rabbit hole that was created by the 11-day lag between the occurrence of the collision on a public roadway and the coordinated disclosure of it. Some of those folks have opted to direct frustration at those who have called the situation as they see it. Why not direct some of that attention to finding out exactly what happened? Like Cohn is doing.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Luke Kuechly will be Netflix's No. 1 game analyst
summary: Next month, linebacker Luke Kuechly will enter the Hall of Fame.
full_text: Next month, linebacker Luke Kuechly will enter the Hall of Fame. The following month, he'll enter the broadcast booth. Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that Kuechly will be Netflix’s No. 1 game analyst this year . Kuechly will debut in the land of the kookaburra on September 10, for Netflix's broadcast of the 49ers-Rams Week 1 contest from Australia. He auditioned for the job earlier this month, at the NBC Sports studios in Stamford, Connecticut. Per Marchand, Kuechly showed "immediate chemistry" with Noah Eagle, and the Netflix executives liked the idea of bringing a fresh, new name into the booth. Kuechly will work four games in all this year, since two of the Netflix games will be played on Christmas Day. And while it's only four games for 2026, Netflix's contract runs through 2029. If Netflix decides to jump in the pool for a full-season package as of 2030, Kuechly would be in prime position to be their primary analyst. The 35-year-old Kuechly has called Panthers radio games, so he has some experience in this space. He'll step onto a massive platform when he shows up in Melbourne.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ohio State lands a record jersey patch deal
summary: When college football season begins, the complaints will follow.
full_text: When college football season begins, the complaints will follow. And they'll be loud. More and more major programs are putting ads on their uniforms . Ohio State, via Sports Business Journal, has landed a record deal with JPMorgan Chase. In exchange for putting the Chase brand on the jerseys of the 36 Ohio State sports programs, the school will get more than $15 million per year. Per SBJ , that's more than twice some of the highest-paying deals. By way of comparison, Monster is paying $20 million annually to the entire Big 12 conference . The folks at SBJ have a database of the current jersey deals . It's a growing list. When fans start seeing them during college football games, there will be huffing and puffing. But no one will be boycotting the house down. Which makes it just a matter of time before the NFL embraces the reality of significant revenue for sewing a patch onto a shirt.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Carter, Eagles agree to four-year extension
summary: The deal will reportedly make Carter the highest-paid DT in league history.
full_text: ' One of the league's top young defenders has just gotten paid. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter and the Eagles have agreed to a four-year extension, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The initial numbers indicate the deal is for $152 million and worth up to $160 million, including $106 million guaranteed. That makes Carter the highest-paid defensive tackle in league history. Carter, whose fifth-year option was exercised earlier this offseason, is now under contract with Philadelphia through 2031. The No. 9 overall pick of the 2023 draft, Carter was instrumental in helping the Eagles win Super Bowl LIX to cap the 2024 season. In his three years, Carter has registered 13.5 sacks, 25 tackles for loss, and 37 quarterback hits in 43 games with 27 starts. A two-time Pro Bowler, he’s also tallied 13 passes defensed and four forced fumbles.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Denzel Ward agrees to extension with Browns, regains status as highest-paid DB in NFL history, per report
summary: Ward already topped the cornerback earnings leaderboard when he signed his previous deal
full_text:
Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward is the highest-paid defensive back in NFL history. Again. Ward agreed to a two-year, $62.2 million extension with the Browns that includes $52.3 million in guaranteed money, according to ESPN and NFL Media .
This is the second time in Ward's career that he has reset the cornerback market. In 2022, he signed a five-year, $100.5 million extension that runs through 2027. With the new extension in effect, Ward will be tied to the Browns through 2029.
The vast majority of NFL veterans reported to training camp on Tuesday, and with their return to team facilities came a flurry of contract agreements. Ward is the third Pro Bowler of the day to come to terms with his team on a massive deal. Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter became the highest-paid player at his position when he secured a four-year, $152 million deal, and Minnesota Vikings offensive lineman Brian O'Neill is set to sign for four more years at $96 million.
Ward is the seventh defensive back to land a deal with an average annual value of at least $25 million. Below are the others, along with their rankings by contract value.
Contract data via Over The Cap
As one of the primary catalysts behind the Browns' ferocious defense a year ago, Ward earned his fifth Pro Bowl selection in eight years and made it eight consecutive seasons with an interception to open his stellar career. He is just two years removed from leading the NFL with 19 passes defended in 2024 and has become a more steady presence of late, missing just three games over the past two seasons.
Ward, an Ohio native and a product of Ohio State, has effectively been everything the Browns could have hoped for when they kept him in state and selected him with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . Now he will continue to anchor the defensive backfield for at least four more years.
author: Carter Bahns

title: How Buccaneers opened training camp on worst foot possible with cloud of uncertainty
summary: Tampa Bay's training camp opened with Vita Vea requesting a trade and Baker Mayfield poised to play out the final year of his contract
full_text:
The annual opening of training camp typically brings optimism to most NFL teams . Anything is possible. This will be our year. But for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2026, fans did not even have time to digest practice highlights before the first couple of waves of concerning news came ashore.
Recently, Vita Vea made a trade request. The run-stopping force that anchored the Tampa Bay defensive line for the last eight years sought a new contract that would prevent him from hitting free agency next offseason, and he even conducted a hold-in during minicamp in an effort to get a deal across the finish line. Vea and the team could not reach an agreement on an extension in time for camp, and the defensive tackle asked to be traded on the eve of the first practice .
The next day, Baker Mayfield reported to camp without a new deal of his own. The quarterback self-imposed a July 28 deadline to wrap up negotiations, and the situation looked bleak all summer after Mayfield said in early June that the sides were not close to an agreement .
While the Mayfield negotiations are not as dire as Vea's, the momentum is moving toward 2026 being the quarterback's final year with Tampa Bay. Mayfield intends to play out the last year of his contract and become an unrestricted free agent at the start of the 2027 league year, a ccording to ESPN . He is reportedly unfazed by the possibility of the Buccaneers using the franchise tag to keep him around for another year.
Mayfield reportedly seeks a pay bump that would put his earnings more in line with those of similarly talented quarterbacks. The $33.3 million average annual salary on his present contract makes him the 16th-highest-paid signal-caller in the league. He ranked 18th in QBR in his first year with the team, 13th in 2024 and 12th last year.
Just because they did not agree on Mayfield's timeline does not mean they will not strike a deal before next spring, though. Franchise legend Mike Evans found himself in a similar boat three years ago and ultimately finalized an extension after playing out the 2023 season. But either the Buccaneers do not envision Mayfield as their long-term quarterback at his desired price, or they are willing to slow-play the process and risk changes to his value or their relationship.
These contract standoffs at the start of training camp are a dark cloud over what could be a decent year for a team that was squarely in the mix for the wide-open NFC South last year. They also continue a concerning trend that could lead to the roster's core crumbling and the coaching staff falling apart.
Three other developments in particular preceded Mayfield's and Vea's failed contract talks.
Coach Todd Bowles seemed to have worn out his welcome with the fanbase, and the seven losses in nine games to conclude the 2025 season raised questions about his players' buy-in, too. Still, the Buccaneers elected to keep him in place for another year , provided he made changes to his assistant coaching staff. Coming off an 8-9 season that disintegrated over the second half, everything is trending in the wrong direction for him. His job security is perhaps the one to monitor the closest as this year progresses, and if Tampa Bay moves on from him during or after the season, the question will be why it did not make the move sooner.
The greatest wide receiver in franchise history -- and perhaps the greatest offensive player the Buccaneers have ever produced -- could have returned for 2026 if he wanted to. Mike Evans' agent said in a March statement that the team aggressively pursued retaining him and presented him with a highly competitive offer. But in the end, the decision was not about the money, according to his agent. Evans' departure was a red flag, as it signaled his belief that he had a better chance of winning elsewhere.
About two weeks after Evans left town, Lavonte David announced his retirement . Two all-time Tampa Bay greats were gone in close succession. David remained highly productive through his final year at age 35 and left a gaping hole in the middle of the defense, but more concerning than the need to replace his steady presence is the fact that two faces of the franchise decided now was the right time to move on.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Kyle Shanahan injured in car accident: 49ers coach says it was his fault
summary: Reports say Shanahan suffered a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand, a concussion and required more than 40 stitches to his face after the July 14 crash
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have officially reported to training camp but will begin building the foundation for the 2026 campaign with their head coach limited. The team announced in a statement Saturday that Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week and suffered non-life-threatening injuries.
Shanahan, 46, will still participate in team activities, but on a limited basis. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster and the team coordinators will handle the bulk of the head coach duties while Shanahan recuperates. In a press conference on Saturday, 49ers general manager John Lynch told reporters that he does not expect Shanahan to miss Week 1 of the regular season.
Here is the full official statement from the 49ers:
"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care.
Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."
The accident occurred July 14 when Shanahan collided with an SUV near his Northern California home, per ESPN . While the injuries weren't life-threatening, they were significant. ESPN reported that Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs and his hand, suffered a severe concussion and needed more than 40 stitches to his face.
According to Shanahan's close friend, former NFL quarterback Chris Simms, Shanahan was also close to losing his right eye in the accident.
"So just to let you know, paint the picture, you've seen the injury report, the broken ribs, 40 stitches in the face, the broken nose, broken left hand. Of course, the bad concussion. But when you first see it, and it's fresh, and some of the cuts are still wide open, I mean, it's jarring. It's jarring," Simms said on PFT Live .
"He was this close to maybe losing his right eye, right? The scar is so big right here. And so all that stuff was just crazy to see. And, of course, I was thinking of my friend, but yeah, it's tough. And he's still battling with this concussion. . . . He's healing. His face looks a whole lot better, but this concussion, of course, being a part of that kind of accident is lingering and it's giving him issues, and he's certainly still dealing with that."
Shanahan on Tuesday called a group of reporters into his office to clarify certain circumstances of the crash . He said that the state database mishandled some of the details and, importantly, that it was him who crossed into oncoming traffic and not the 21-year-old driver of the other vehicle. Shanahan recounted that his phone slipped out of his lap and that he went to reach for it. When he sat back up, the airbag deployed.
Despite his concussion and significant injuries to his face, Shanahan said he never lost consciousness and that he remembered the crash clearly.
Shanahan was taken by paramedics to a local hospital and released later the day of the accident. The other driver was not injured, according to Palo Alto Lt. Nicholas Martinez. He also told ESPN that drugs and alcohol were not involved, and both drivers cooperated with law enforcement.
Since the crash, Shanahan has been recovering at home and informed the coaching staff of the incident on Tuesday. He has yet to be cleared by doctors for full coaching duties and won't be until his concussion symptoms subside.
Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, who worked with Shanahan when they were assistants in Washington, said he's spoken to the 49ers coach since the car accident. McVay, a fellow NFC West coach, said Shanahan has a great perspective on the accident and on his recovery.
"I have talked to him. My thoughts and prayers are with him and his family, and I know he's got an incredible perspective on it all. And Kyle's a stud. I have as much respect for him as anybody and he's a friend of mine, and I love him and hope that he's going to have a great recovery," McVay said .
McVay expressed gratitude that the accident didn't have a worse outcome and noted that Shanahan's approach to his recovery is similar to how coaches run a team.
"Most importantly, thank God he and the other person involved are okay. Perspective is everything. We talk about that all the time as coaches, and everybody goes through different things," McVay said. "I think the most important thing is that he's on the road to recovery. His wife Mandy, and he's got a beautiful family, and I think any time that something like that happens, it shakes you up a little bit."
Shanahan is entering his 10th season as the 49ers' head coach. Since being hired in 2017, he has become one of the league's top coaches, compiling an 82-67 (.550) regular-season record and a 9-5 playoff mark. Under his leadership, San Francisco has made two Super Bowl appearances and is coming off a 12-5 regular-season campaign in 2025 that ended with a divisional-round loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Highest-paid players at every NFL position: A look at who is cashing the biggest check heading into 2026
summary: A look at the markets by position for 2026
full_text:
The NFL offseason is almost over, and we've already seen some big moves and changes. Free agency and the NFL Draft are behind us, and with training camp approaching, we can practically smell the pigskin and taste the tailgate food that soon awaits.
It's no secret that the NFL is a money-making machine: from merchandise, to commercials, streaming services to tickets and more. Money is often a big hurdle between teams and players, with contract holdouts, hold-ins and trades giving each season plenty of drama on the sidelines.
The NFL salary cap has more than doubled in the last decade-plus and now sits at over $300 million per team heading into 2026. Some teams are known to be more willing to spend money, while others like to be more cautious with the paycheck.
Some players decide to take less to be on the team they want, or to regain a solid core around them, while others demand the highest value at their position. Just who are the ones taking home the biggest bag?
We broke down the highest-paid players by position, based on average annual value, to get a feel for where the market stands. All values are via Spotrac .
Patrick Mahomes agreed this offseason to terms on a revised contract that adds two years to his existing deal and makes him the highest-paid quarterback in average annual value. The three-time Super Bowl MVP and two-time NFL MVP is the first player in NFL history to sign a contract worth more than $500 million. He passed Dak Prescott , who previously held the title at $60 million per year. Followed by Mahomes and Prescott are Josh Allen , Joe Burrow , Trevor Lawrence , Jordan Love and Matthew Stafford , who all hold $55 million AAV deals, according to Spotrac.
Saquon Barkley earned his payday after a historic 2024 season, where he not only earned NFL Offensive Player of the Year, an All-Pro honor and was the rushing leader, but he also took home a Super Bowl ring. Barkley was pivotal in the Super Bowl run, setting the league record for most rushing yards in a single season (2,504), including playoffs.
The 32-year-old went undrafted in 2017 before signing with the Baltimore Ravens . He signed with the Giants this offseason after earning Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors in 2025.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba was essential in the Seahawks ' Super Bowl champion run last season, as the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year. He had 119 receptions and 1,793 receiving yards, a league high, along with 10 touchdowns in the regular season. His breakout year came at the perfect time for Sam Darnold's offense and he has high expectations as he enters Year 4.
George Kittle is arguably the best tight end in the league right now and it shows in his contract. The seven-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro has spent his entire career with the 49ers . Kittle started and ended his season with injuries last year, missing five games due to a hamstring tear suffered in Week 1 and going down with an Achilles injury in their wild card game against the Eagles . He still has goals of a Week 1 return for the 2026 season.
Laremy Tunsil was the No. 13 overall pick in 2016, selected by the Miami Dolphins . He then went to the Houston Texans before joining the Commanders in 2025. His resume includes five Pro Bowl honors and he has started all 139 games he's played in.
Tyler Smith beats out last year's highest-paid offensive guard Trey Smith , who earns an average of $23.5 million per year. The 2022 No. 24 overall pick has become pivotal on the Cowboys ' line and has three Pro Bowls during his time in the league.
Tyler Linderbaum was drafted No. 25 overall in 2022 by the Ravens, where he remained until this offseason when he joined the Raiders . The three-time Pro Bowler took 99% of offensive snaps last season, starting all 17 games.
Will Anderson Jr . became the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history with his massive three-year, $150 million deal. According to Next Gen Stats, he was seventh in run-stop rate (12.6%), third in run stuffs (13) and second in pressures (85) among defenders with at least 150 run defensive snaps in 2025. His performance put him second in NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting. He was named DPOY in 2023.
Jeffery Simmons briefly held the title of highest-paid interior defensive lineman this offseason before Jalen Carter took the throne with a huge extension on the eve of the first practice of training camp. Carter's extension doesn't kick in until after the 2027 season and includes $106 million guaranteed.
Fred Warner has spent his entire career with the Niners and the team has him under contract until 2030. He is a four-time first-team All-Pro and a four-time Pro Bowler, starting all 121 regular-season and 12 playoff games he's appeared in. The defensive leader was limited to six games last season due to an ankle fracture.
Trent McDuffie will make his Rams debut next season after spending his first four seasons with the Chiefs , where he won two Super Bowls. Since he was selected at No. 21 overall in 2022, he has 246 tackles, 34 pass deflections, eight forced fumbles, 5.5 sacks and three interceptions.
Derwin James has played for the Chargers since the team selected him No. 17 overall in 2018. He earned his fifth Pro Bowl and fourth second-team All-Pro honor last season. He had a career-best three interceptions last season, to go with 94 combined tackles, seven passes defended, two sacks and one forced fumble.
This marks the largest deal for a kicker in league history, earned in thanks to Pro Bowls in each of his three seasons in the NFL. Aubrey went undrafted in 2022 and joined the USFL, becoming a two-time champion in the league, before heading to the Cowboys in 2023. He has made 88.2% of field goals attempted and 96.9% of attempted extra points. He has six total field goals over 60 yards, an NFL record.
Jordan Stout led the league with a net average of 44.9 yards last season and earned a Pro Bowl spot due to his 2025 performance.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: 2026 NFL Draft first-round pick contract tracker: Ty Simpson signs deal with Rams to round out class
summary: A rundown of the rookie contracts for the first-round picks of the 2026 class
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Draft is a thing of the past, and now it's time for the 257 selected players to join their teams by signing rookie contracts. Rookies can participate in minicamps and other offseason activities while not under contract, but once training camp rolls around, they need to be under contract to avoid complications.
Complications do indeed happen. Signing a rookie deal is usually a formality, with the rookie wage scale from the 2011 NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement laying out non-negotiable salary slots for the rookie wage scale. Still, there are a few instances in which things get sticky -- Shemar Stewart last offseason stands out as one such example -- and as such, it's worth keeping track of who has officially signed and who hasn't.
It took until hours before training camp began, but Ty Simpson rounded out the group, signing his deal with the Rams on July 25, the day the team reported to camp. No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza, also a quarterback, signed a few days before.
Below is the contract status for all 32 first-round picks, with all salary numbers via Spotrac .
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Eagles make Jalen Carter highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history with $152 million extension, per report
summary: Carter resets the market and gets $106 million guaranteed
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are rewarding another one of their homegrown talents, as the franchise has agreed on a four-year, $152 million extension with Jalen Carter to make him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history, per ESPN . The deal is reportedly worth up to $160 million, with $106 million guaranteed. Carter is now under contract through the 2031 season.
Carter's new AAV of $38 million per year resets the defensive tackle market one month after it was topped by Jeffery Simmons of the Tennessee Titans . Simmons received a three-year deal worth $105.8 million after leading all defensive tackles last season with 11.0 sacks while picking up First Team All-Pro honors. However, Carter is four years younger than Simmons at 25-years-old.
The Eagles now have two of the top six highest-paid defensive tackles in the NFL, as they signed Carter's running mate Jordan Davis to a three-year, $78 million deal in March.
Milton Williams , Patriots
Quinnen Williams , Cowboys
The Eagles selected Carter with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Georgia. He has made back-to-back Pro Bowls over the last two seasons, and has established himself as one of the best up-and-coming interior stars the league has to offer.
While Carter played in just 11 games this past season, really 10 when you consider he was ejected just seconds into the season-opening win against the Cowboys for his actions toward Dak Prescott , he recorded 33 tackles, three sacks, 12 QB hits and seven passes defensed. In 43 career games over three seasons, Carter has recorded 108 tackles, 13.5 sacks and four forced fumbles. His 25 career tackles for loss are the fourth-most through a defensive tackle's first three seasons since 2010, behind Geno Atkins (29), Ndamukong Suh (36) and Aaron Donald (57).
The Eagles should be confident they have one of the best interior defensive lines in the NFL with Carter, Davis and Moro Ojomo , but the pass rush is a different issue.
Philly lost Jaelan Phillips in free agency after acquiring him at the trade deadline last year. He signed a four-year, $120 million deal with the Panthers that was the most lucrative contract signed in free agency. He registered the fourth-highest pressure rate (18.8%) in the league this past season. With him on the field, the Eagles had the fifth-highest pressure rate with the lowest blitz rate.
After losing Phillips, Philly traded for Jonathan Greenard . He's recorded at least 12 sacks in two out of the last three seasons, and had an 18.1% pressure rate in 2025, which ranked No. 7 in the NFL. Greenard is going to be one of the Eagles' starting pass rushers, with his running mate to be determined. That should be Nolan Smith Jr. or Jalyx Hunt .
Smith got to the quarterback three times in 12 starts last season. The former No. 30 overall pick has recorded just 10.5 sacks over his three NFL seasons, but did have the fifth-year option exercised on his rookie contract. Hunt on the other hand led the Eagles with 6.5 sacks and three interceptions this past season, to go along with 52 tackles. The former defensive back turned pass rusher was more productive than Smith, and actually became the first player to ever lead a team outright in sacks and interceptions, per CBS Sports Research
The magician Howie Roseman found a way to extend both Carter and Davis and solidify the interior of Philly's defensive line for years to come. It's an expensive investment at $230 million, but the Eagles are going to face a similar dilemma next year!
The Eagles found two star secondary players in the 2024 NFL Draft with cornerback Quinyon Mitchell at No. 22 overall, and then the versatile Cooper DeJean at No. 40 overall. Both will be extension eligible next offseason. Mitchell has the fifth-year option in his contract, DeJean does not.
Mitchell is coming off a campaign in which he was named First Team All-Pro and made the Pro Bowl after recording 45 tackles and 17 passes defensed. He led all defensive backs with a 39.6% completion percentage allowed, and did not surrender a single touchdown in coverage. DeJean was also named First Team All-Pro, and allowed zero touchdowns in coverage from the slot while snagging two interceptions. He also recorded four tackles for loss, which were the most by an Eagles defensive back.
Both of these players are top 10 talents at their position, and both should be looking to reset the market that is about to be first reset by Christian Gonzalez and Devon Witherspoon . There's a full season of football left to be played before we get there, but it's something for Eagles fans to consider.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Ranking the seven worst NFL uniforms of all-time after Bills' new 'Nickel City' alternate gets ripped by fans
summary: The Bills' new alternate uniforms were bad, but not as bad as these seven combinations
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills might have done the impossible. it's hard to get everyone on the internet to agree on anything, but everyone definitely seems to agree on one thing this week and that's the fact that the Bills might have just released the worst alternate uniform of all-time.
If you missed it, the Bills unveiled a new "Nickel City" alternate on Monday that features a gray jersey and gray pants paired with a blue helmet. It marks the first time in franchise history that the Bills have worn a gray jersey or a blue helmet.
Bills unveil new alternate "Nickel City" uniforms 🔥 Thoughts on the Buffalo Bills new jerseys? 😯 (📸: @BuffaloBills ) pic.twitter.com/JIe8dSxQde
Based on fan reaction, the Bills probably should have kept this uniform combo in the closet.
Let's get a quick reaction from fans:
Who designed these? Some college intern with no business in designing a pro football uniform? Goodness, they look like something straight outta the arena league. Your 2002-2010 duds put these costumes to shame, and that's a tough act to follow.
the gray is terrible but other than that I hate it
Temu jersey your uncle gets you before never speaking to the family again
This is the worst part for me. I saw this and felt immediate anger. These look like Power Ranger helmets! #BuffaloBills #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/m1lDbI4z6R
You know fans are upset when you have the Blue Power Ranger out here catching strays.
Based on fan reaction, it seems the Bills probably should have put a few Focus Groups together before deciding to go with an all-gray look.
I gave the new uniform a C+ during a segment on CBS Sports HQ on Monday night (You can see it here ). I like the blue helmets, but I don't like the logo on the helmet, and I don't like the blue paired with the gray. As a matter of fact, I would have loved to see the blue helmet with any other jersey color. I also think gray pants could have worked with a non-gray jersey. This was just a one bad fashion decision after another.
With the Bills getting ripped by nearly everyone for this new alternate look, it got me wondering whether this will go down as one of the worst uniforms of all time, and right now, it's certainly possible.
Here's my ranking of the worst throwback/alternate uniforms of all-time:
When your starting quarterback comes out and says he hates your uniform, then it's probably a bad uniform, and that's exactly what happened in 2015 when the Jaguars unveiled their Color Rush uniform.
Uniforms Jaguars will wear next Thursday night vs Titans pic.twitter.com/wJESUEYHOZ
Officially, the Jags were wearing a color called "Bold Gold," but to anyone with two eyes, it was pretty clear this was more of an all-mustard look that should have never left the drawing board. Blake Bortles, who was the Jaguars QB at the time, hated the fact that he had to wear the mustard-colored uniforms.
"I think they're ugly as hell," Bortles said at the time . "I am not a big fan of the mustard. ... I think they should choose a different color."
It's possible that someday, we'll see someone combine a mustard jersey with gray pants, but until that happens, this will remain as the worst alternate/throwback jersey of all time.
I'm not the first person to rank the ugliest uniforms in NFL history, and I certainly won't be the last, and if there's one thing that all of these lists have in common, it's that the Eagles' 1934 throwback is always in the ranking. It's the modern standard for ugliest throwback.
During the 2007 season, the Eagles decided to celebrate their 75th anniversary by wearing their 1934 uniforms. There are only two seasons in Eagles history where the team didn't wear green, and 1934 was one of them. During their first two years of existence, the Eagles wore a gold and baby blue jersey.
Eagles 1934 throwbacks. Hideous, glorious or both? pic.twitter.com/q3nvOTcZXS
Throwing it back to when we wore the 75th anniversary yellow and blue jerseys. pic.twitter.com/3WAQkIlbYA
As the Chargers have proven, these two colors can make an amazing uniform, but not when combined. If the Eagles had gone with just baby blue or just gold, they might have been able to put together a solid uniform combo, but instead, they combined the colors and came up with this hideous mishmash.
I know 2032 is still six years away, but I'm already dreading it just knowing that the Eagles might once again break these out for the team's 100th anniversary.
When the owner of the team decides that he needs to set every uniform on fire to burn them out of existence, then you probably have a bad uniform, and that's exactly what happened with the next uniform on our list. During the Broncos' first two years of existence, they wore a yellow jersey over Brown pants. If there are two colors you should never combine under any circumstance, it's brown and yellow.
After the Broncos switched to their orange and blue uniforms in 1963, the team decided to get rid of their old uniforms by burning them.
From the Broncos' website : "The home combination — a mustard-yellow jersey with brown numbers and no name block, brown pants with mustard-yellow double stripes, and brown and yellow vertically striped socks — was so hated that a public bonfire was held by the team in front of a cheering crowd to burn the uniforms."
Although the uniforms were hated, the Broncos brought them back in 2009 and wore them for the AFL's 50th anniversary season.
AFL Denver Broncos is by far the worst throwback.  The socks make them look like oompah-loompah's. pic.twitter.com/VDoSjAKI2h
Currently re watching the #Broncos 2009 win over the #Patriots and I forgot how fun this game was besides the horrendous AFL throwback jerseys. The atmosphere was electric with the #Broncos being 4-0 at the time. pic.twitter.com/OtcjSHa8LL
The Broncos also had a white version of these throwback uniforms, and those were much better. As for the yellow ones, I hope the team decides to have another bonfire to get rid of them.
I'm not sure what was going on in Pennsylvania in 1934, but it almost seems like the Steelers and Eagles were competing to see who could design the worst jersey. The Eagles' 1934 throwbacks came in at No. 2 on this list, and now we have the Steelers' 1934 throwbacks ranked fourth ugliest.
These are the famous bumblebee jerseys that the Steelers wore for five games between 2012 and 2016.
The most famously terrible uniforms: the bumblebee Steelers uniforms. pic.twitter.com/rOv3pB7eZ3
Putting horizontal prison stripes on an NFL uniform just seems like a bad idea. I think my biggest problem with this uniform is that the pants don't make any sense.
