title: 2026 Saints: New Season, New Roster, New Leaders
summary: Last season, the New Orleans Saints featured eight captains: three on offense, three on defense, and two on special teams. Of the eight captains from last year’s team, five of them will be returning, but that does not necessarily mean all five will be voted team captains again. The Saints saw a midseason departure from […]
full_text: Last season, the New Orleans Saints featured eight captains: three on offense, three on defense, and two on special teams. Of the eight captains from last year’s team, five of them will be returning, but that does not necessarily mean all five will be voted team captains again. The Saints saw a midseason departure from Brandin Cooks, a change at kicker with Blake Grupe, and Demario Davis opted to return to the Jets in the offseason. Since then, a lot has changed for this Saints roster. There has been an influx of youth, but also an increase in talent. And with talent comes hope. But that talent still needs to be led. Let’s begin with the obvious. Out of all the circumstances surrounding this offseason, it’s easy to believe that Cam Jordan will remain a team captain. He was first named a captain ahead of the 2015 season, and the “C” has not left his jersey since. Staying on the defensive side of the ball, I can also see Justin Reid remaining a captain. Last season was the first time in his career Reid was named a captain, and you can hear from his teammates and coaches how much they value his intelligence, guidance, his drive to motivate the defense, and his ability to back it up with his play on the field. With Demario Davis leaving for the Jets, I can see the Saints selecting Kaden Ellis to become the next long-standing captain at the linebacker position. Ellis returns to the Saints after spending multiple seasons in Atlanta. Having started his career with the Saints—even though it was under a different coaching staff at the time—Ellis is still thought of highly throughout the organization and by the players who were here when he began. Flipping to the offensive side of the ball, I see the Saints sticking with center Erik McCoy as the captain along the offensive line. McCoy has been a captain for the past three seasons, and now that this group is beginning to take shape with the addition of David Edwards and the emergence of the two young tackles, it makes sense for him to remain a leader of the offensive unit. Now, this is where things can get really fun. With the return of Alvin Kamara, I believe the Saints will name Kamara a captain once again. Kamara was first named a captain in 2022 but was not selected in 2023. Heading into the 2024 season, he was selected again and remained a captain through this past season. With the addition of Travis Etienne Jr., I could see the hometown hero emerging as a leader on the offense, as he was a two-time captain in Jacksonville over the past two seasons. However, I can also see the Saints shifting toward wide receiver Chris Olave, who has shown a lot of growth and maturity over the past few years. If I had to make the pick, I believe the Saints will put the “C” on the jersey of their newest offensive acquisition, Travis Etienne Jr. When it comes to the special teams unit, I believe the Saints may select punter Ryan Wright, whom they signed this offseason. This is an addition that I don’t think is being discussed enough, and I would not be surprised at all if Wright jogs onto the field for pregame warmups in September with a “C” on his jersey. Zach Wood would be the other special teams selection. Wood has been a captain for the past three seasons, and it would make sense for him to remain one. That gives us a total of seven captains, leaving one remaining spot on the offensive side of the ball. I think this should be the most obvious choice: Tyler Shough. Shough has done everything you want to see, not just from a young quarterback entering his first full offseason as the guy, but also as the face of the franchise. He has not only set the tone for the team but for the community as a whole. He represents the city extremely well, and every time he steps in front of a camera or microphone, he has not missed. Since offseason workouts began, he has been the one organizing the group, bringing teammates together to train and build chemistry. He even paid for their recent trip to California to work out with Saints legend Drew Brees. Keep in mind, Shough is still on his rookie contract. The second-year quarterback has been a major reason why so much hope is flooding back into the fan base, and it’s time for Tyler Shough to step into the leadership role this organization has been missing since No. 9 walked off the field. With Brees gone for the past several seasons, Demario Davis now in New York, and Cam Jordan entering what is essentially his farewell season, the succession of leadership should fall directly to Tyler Shough. This will be a big year for the young quarterback, both on and off the field. Just to recap: Defense: Cam Jordan, Justin Reid, Kaden Ellis Offense: Erik McCoy, Travis Etienne Jr., Tyler Shough Special Teams: Zach Wood and Ryan Wright Who do you think will be the Saints’ captains for the upcoming season?
author: Anthony Parker

title: Drew Brees sees bright future for Tyler Shough, Saints’ rebuilt offense
summary: With the New Orleans Saints officially entering a new era at quarterback, no one understands the demands of leading the franchise better than Pro Football Hall of Famer Drew Brees. In an exclusive one-on-one interview with Covers.com, the future Hall of Famer sat down with DJ Siddiqi to discuss the Saints’ outlook under quarterback Tyler Shough, […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JULY 11: Drew Brees announces a light heavyweight fight during the UFC 329 event at T-Mobile Arena on July 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) With the New Orleans Saints officially entering a new era at quarterback, no one understands the demands of leading the franchise better than Pro Football Hall of Famer Drew Brees. In an exclusive one-on-one interview with Covers.com , the future Hall of Famer sat down with DJ Siddiqi to discuss the Saints’ outlook under quarterback Tyler Shough, who enters his second season and first as the team’s Week 1 starter. Brees praised the young signal-caller’s maturity, poise and leadership while expressing optimism about the direction of the offense under head coach Kellen Moore. “I’ve been really impressed with him,” Brees said. “I talked to him around the draft last year, at training camp, during the season and right before he took over.” Brees said he watched the Saints gradually come together despite facing significant changes on both sides of the football. “To watch that team come together—in a lot of ways it was a new offense with Kellen Moore, it was a new defense with Brandon Staley—but man, they really hit their stride at the end of the year, and in large part, the quarterback was playing well.” The Saints legend believes Shough possesses many of the physical and mental traits needed to succeed at the professional level. “Tyler, he’s a big, strong athlete, mature beyond his years, plays with great poise. Strong arm. He can run the ball well, creates some versatility as an offense.” With another offseason in Moore’s system, Brees expects Shough to take another step in his development in 2026. “I think he’s got some natural leadership ability. The guys seem to gravitate to him.” That said, Brees believes continuity could be one of New Orleans’ biggest advantages entering the season. “And now in his second year in the offense, you add a weapon like Jordyn Tyson to go along with Chris Olave and some of the other guys that they have—Juwan Johnson, Alvin Kamara’s coming back, and you go out and sign Travis Etienne.” The collection of offensive playmakers gives New Orleans plenty of reasons for optimism. “You’ve got some weapons and guys to spread the ball to that are real playmakers,” Brees said. “But it’s all about the guy pulling the trigger making great decisions and putting everybody in positions to succeed.” For Brees, that’s the next challenge for Shough. The supporting cast appears to be in place. Now it’s about the quarterback making the right reads, distributing the football efficiently and elevating the players around him. Given Brees’ intimate knowledge of what it takes to succeed in New Orleans, his endorsement carries considerable weight. While expectations surrounding Shough remain measured, one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history sees a player with the physical tools, leadership qualities and offensive support necessary to help lead the Saints into their next chapter.

title: NY Giants news: Giants report to West Virginia for training camp
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Wednesday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp. Giants camp in W.Va.: Cool temps, plush grounds and some football | ESPN.com The Greenbrier boasts a state-of-the-art performance center, built in 2014, that has a locker room and multiple fields conducive to […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Wednesday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp. Giants camp in W.Va.: Cool temps, plush grounds and some football | ESPN.com The Greenbrier boasts a state-of-the-art performance center, built in 2014, that has a locker room and multiple fields conducive to hosting an NFL team for training camp. o, New York will take its training camp on the road for 12 days to West Virginia. It was a decision that was in the works before new coach John Harbaugh was hired. And the Greenbrier meets the Giants’ needs with two grass fields, a turf option (in case of rain), meeting rooms, offices, a weight room, player and coach locker rooms, a training room, a hydrotherapy room and an equipment room. The conditions are also conducive to a comfortable training camp. Temperatures usually range from the low 60s to around 80 degrees with low humidity in the mountains of West Virginia — cooler than the swamps of New Jersey. BBV’s Ed Valentine is on the scene Welcome to the Greenbrier practice facility. #NYG pic.twitter.com/9aNuiVvHIB — Big Blue View (@bigblueview) July 28, 2026 Vita Vea landing spots: Eight possible destinations for Buccaneers DT after trade request | NFL.com The need is clear after Big Blue traded Dexter Lawrence — perhaps the only current nose tackle better than Vea — this offseason. D.J. Reader is a solid veteran who can plug a hole, but he’s no Vea. It would take some work to fit Vea under the cap, but that shouldn’t be a prohibitor in the year of our Lord 2026 — of course, if the Giants didn’t want to pay Lawrence, they might balk at this scenario as well. Perhaps the Bucs would be interested in a Kayvon Thibodeaux swap? Vea playing alongside the likes of Brian Burns and Abdul Carter would provide a lethal front. Vea’s presence would also help clog the lanes for rookie Arvell Reese to torpedo in from the second level. Giants training camp preview: Why N.Y. decided to keep Malik Nabers off PUP list | The Athletic The Giants have been targeting a Week 1 return for Nabers, so they obviously didn’t prioritize the ability to potentially shift him to the reserve/PUP list. And even if Nabers isn’t ready for the opener, the Giants can evaluate him weekly rather than locking in a four-game absence. Of course, the Giants are hoping Nabers’ earlier start to practice this summer has him ready for Week 1. Avoiding the PUP list was a promising first step, but it’s not the final checkpoint. It will be a gradual process for Nabers and, barring any setbacks, it’s fair to be optimistic that he’ll be in the lineup against the Cowboys. 5 big questions as Giants open camp in West Virginia | New York Daily News Is Jaxson Dart The Guy? Everything about the Giants’ fortunes in the 2026 NFL season centers around the ability of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart to grow as a pocket passer and a game manager and finisher. Dart, 23, has a lot on his plate to accomplish that. He is learning a new offense under a new coach and coordinator. He is in the public spotlight on the political side now after aligning with Donald Trump, which puts a different kind of spotlight on a young player who needs fewer distractions. Year 1 of Harbaugh’s program must be viewed as the beginning of a rebuild and turnaround that is not going to happen overnight. Dart, though, controls whether or not 2026 brings immediate promise in the team’s current core or if it demonstrates there is even more work to do than Harbaugh had hoped when he took the job. Exclusive: 2x Super Bowl champion Phil Simms on Jaxson Dart, John Harbaugh and the Giants prospects | Casino.org “It’s so huge to have that guy. I’ve been over there, and when John Harbaugh is in front of that group and they sit in that little theatre there with the lectern in front and Harbs comes in through that side door, trust me, everyone sits up straight and they’re a little bit nervous, because they know he’s the man and he is in charge. “But how he presents himself to the team, I’m just a big believer in him. He’s like Parcells. It didn’t matter if I had a great game or not; he’d come walk in that side door and he’d throw a pen on lectern and it was, not really fear, but he commanded your attention. What he’s creating there is a really good thing for that team.” Albert Breer’s Takeaways: With Fernando Mendoza Signed, the Raiders’ Positive Momentum Continues | SI..com Predictably, [John Harbaugh] got roasted on social media, because social media is a cynical place. But, again, this is in line with who Harbaugh is and what he built over 18 years in Baltimore. It reflected his reverence for the game’s history and, obviously, the Giants’ place in it—and that was indeed a real factor in why he picked New York over the other options he had in January. It also showed what he wants his players to establish, which is almost a college-like pride in the program they’re about to build. Bottom line, over 18 years, it wasn’t tough to identify what his Ravens were. My fourth-grader could spell it out. Big, tough, rugged, resourceful and smart. And it matches, in many ways, what the Giants’ best teams over the past half-century or so have been. So passing that mantle of Giants history on to the players in an effort to build a program that resembles the type he had in Baltimore makes all the sense in the world. Was the delivery of the message a little old-timey? Maybe. But that’s how the Harbaughs talk, and it’s genuine. And I’d bet, contrary to what people on X think, it works. Happy 23rd birthday, Malik! summary: The New York Giants 2026 training camp is here. The full roster reports Tuesday, as does our own Ed Valentine, and practices will follow soon after. full_text: ﻿New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh speaks to the media. | Getty Images The New York Giants 2026 training camp is here. The full roster reports Tuesday, as does our own Ed Valentine, and practices will follow soon after. This is, obviously, the first training camp of the John Harbaugh era and it promised to be just a bit different from what we’ve seen in recent years. After all, while the Giants’ roster as a whole hasn’t undergone a total rebuild, there has been a fair amount of turnover as well as new schemes on offense and defense. So with that in mind we wanted to take the temperature of the fanbase: What are you looking forward to in camp this year? Do you want to see what the new offense looks? The Giants will have a new scheme created by Matt Nagy, Brian Callahan, and Greg Roman. Likewise, there is a bevy of new receivers as well as TE Isaiah Likely and FB Patrick Ricard. Do you want to see the new defense under Dennard Wilson? Wilson is expected to bring his own take on the “Ravens 2.0” school, with a new-look defensive front, a (hopefully) improved secondary, and a more aggressive mindset. Do you want to see Jaxson Dart improves (or doesn’t improve) in his second year under the new coaches? The Giants will go as Dart goes, and Harbaugh has raved about Dart’s work ethic this summer. Can he make the leap with the new staff or will he have a sophomore slump? Do you want to see the 2026 rookie class in action? How will Sisi Mauigoa handle the conversion to guard and how the team use Arvell Reese, Colton Hood, and Malachi Fields? Likewise, how will the trio of 6th rounders fare? There are, of course, plenty of storylines to follow this year, Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. title: NY Giants’ Abdul Carter faces big expectations in Year 2
summary: Abdul Carter did not post the production many expected last season after the New York Giants made him the No. 3 overall selection in the 2025 NFL Draft. NFL analysts expect that to change in 2026. Carter was recently named as the Giants’ non-quarterback MVP candidate by Kevin Patra of NFL.com. He wrote: As a […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Abdul Carter did not post the production many expected last season after the New York Giants made him the No. 3 overall selection in the 2025 NFL Draft. NFL analysts expect that to change in 2026. Carter was recently named as the Giants’ non-quarterback MVP candidate by Kevin Patra of NFL.com. He wrote: As a rookie, Carter might have netted just four sacks, but he led Big Blue with 72 QB pressures — seventh-most in the league, per NGS — and a 15.4 percent QB pressure rate. The edge rusher showed improvement down the stretch, logging 3.5 of his four sacks in the final five weeks. With a strong get-off and more seasoning, Carter should put up bigger numbers in 2026. The Giants upgraded the surroundings for new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, which should provide more opportunities for Carter to cause havoc on a consistent basis after ebbs and flows last season. Carter was also named to NFL.com’s All-Under 25 team , this time by Nick Shook. He wrote: Carter arrived with great expectations as a top-three pick and attracted attention for his winding journey toward selecting a jersey number, then seemed to fly under the national radar throughout most of his rookie season. Those paying closer attention, however, understood that Carter had a strong debut campaign. Despite recording just four sacks in 2025, Carter finished seventh in quarterback pressures with 72 (per NGS), just five fewer than Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett recorded. He earned enough Defensive Rookie of the Year votes to finish fifth, and if he can convert more of his pressures into sacks, he’ll quickly climb the popularity charts. He turns 23 in October, too, so he has plenty of time to do so. Valentine’s View Giants fans can only hope these prognostications are right, and that Carter will have a monster season. The talent is unquestionably there for that to happen. The well-documented issues Carter had last season with being late, or missing practices and meetings entirely, were growing pains associated with maturity. A year later, and with an accomplished head coach better equipped to keep him on the right path, Carter could indeed by headed for a breakout season.

title: How hard will John Harbaugh’s NY Giants training camp be?
summary: NFL training camps are not what they used to be. Full two-a-day practices are. So are practices that can drag on as long as the head coach deems necessary. So, when New York Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked during mandatory minicamp how physically and mentally demanding this summer’s training camp will be, he responded […]
full_text: The Greenbrier Resort | Getty Images NFL training camps are not what they used to be. Full two-a-day practices are. So are practices that can drag on as long as the head coach deems necessary. So, when New York Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked during mandatory minicamp how physically and mentally demanding this summer’s training camp will be, he responded with a question of his own: “Is there a rating scale for that? Give me the rating scale. What is the scale?” Harbaugh asked. “Vince Lombardi being 10 and whatever, it won’t be that. It won’t be Lombardi-esque or anything like that.” Would it be an eight if a Vince Lombardi camp was a 10? “I guess it will be 8,” Harbaugh said. Practice rules outlined in the Collective Bargaining Agreement don’t allow anything close to a Vince Lombardi-level practice. Or, even the practices Harbaugh took part in as a young NFL assistant coach. “In the old days, you used to be able to say we’re going to have a great practice no matter how long it takes. There’s a certain motivation to that,” Harbaugh said recently in an exclusive interview with Big Blue View. “I mean, you could be out there three hours, three and a half hours, and at times we were in Philadelphia with Andy Reid. “I mean, we practiced a long time. That was Andy. That was Mike Holmgren. That was Bill Walsh. I mean, these are the great coaches in the NFL. Historically, they’ve had that.” That all went away in the 2011 CBA, forcing coaches to adjust. “The rules are good because the time limit that they put on it is about right,” Harbaugh said. “You can definitely get it done in that amount of time. “You’ve got to be smart about it. But you’ve got to definitely pack the minutes. You’ve got to make the most of the time. When we’re not on the field, like what we tell the guys, is we spend probably more time in practice preparation and more time in practice recovery than any team in the league. There’s no way another team does as much as we do. So if they do, I’d like to see their schedule.” There were obvious differences in the spring from how other recent Giants coaches had run practice: In rookie minicamp, draft picks took reps during team periods. That had not been the case under Brian Daboll. In OTAs and mandatory minicamp, first- and second-team players took the majority of the reps in team drills. Those of us who get to watch practices on occasion have become accustomed to seeing front-line players take a couple of reps and then watch third- and fourth-team players who likely won’t make the roster do much of the work. Practices generally lasted the full amount of time allotted by the CBA. In minicamp, that meant that for the first two days the Giants were on the field for the maximum 2½ hours. “The way the practices are organized, they’re organized to be about, if everything goes perfectly well, you’re looking at, and I’m talking about the long practices, they’re organized to be whatever, like if it’s a two-and-a-half-hour practice, they’re really about 2:10, 2:15 as far as if everything went well,” Harbaugh told Big Blue View. “So there’s a little built-in time for repeated reps, or for extending something out to get it right. “So the idea is it takes a certain amount of time to get it right. We’re not in a hurry to get off the field. We’re in a hurry to get things right.” With Harbaugh, everything is about maximizing each. It is about attacking each day with an “enthusiasm unknown to mankind,” which is something he said in his introductory press conference. A quote that I used in my recent piece on players and coaches reacting to working with Harbaugh is appropriate. “To me, it’s like if it’s worth, if we’re all going to be here, we’re doing something that we feel like is meaningful and important,” Harbaugh said. “Then, to me, that goes through eternity. If you want to look at life that way, which is how I look at it, then let’s go, man. Let’s give it everything we got. Let’s be over the top for that. “We’re not trying to be too cool, too cool for school, or act like this is just another day, or this is like old hat. Nothing is old hat. Everything is new. Everything is a new day, a new opportunity, just to be your best. Talk to them all the time. I mean, being your best is really hard to do. Doing your best is really hard to do. It takes a lot. You got to really be intentional about that.” The schedule for the 10 practices at The Greenbrier hints at what is to come for Giants players. There will be four initial practices, a day off, and then six consecutive days of practice before the team heads back to East Rutherford, N.J. That six-day stretch is the longest allowed by the CBA. Sixteen (16) padded practices are allowed during the preseason. Expect the Giants to use them all. Padded practices are allowed on three consecutive days, with a three-day break in between such padded stretches. Again, no one should be surprised if Harbaugh maximizes chances to use those three-day periods. One thing is certain. West Virginia is not going to be a vacation for anyone around the Giants.

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Monday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp on Wednesday. The New York Giants won’t be a fun obstacle for opposing quarterbacks this offseason. They […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Monday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp on Wednesday. Every NFL Roster’s Biggest Strength and Weakness Before 2026 Preseason | Bleacher Report Biggest Strength: Pass Rush. The New York Giants won’t be a fun obstacle for opposing quarterbacks this offseason. They already had three talented edge-rushers in Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, and they added Ohio State’s Arvell Reese to the group in April. While the Giants plan to use Reese as an off-ball linebacker as a rookie, he will add a new dynamic to the pass rush. Expect to see new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson lead with his pass rush this season. Biggest Weakness: Defensive Tackle. While Dennard should benefit from having a terrific pass-rushing rotation, his group may struggle to control the line of scrimmage. New York’s defensive tackle rotation took a massive hit when Schoen traded Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals, and it took another big one when Roy Robertson-Harris suffered a torn ACL during OTAs. New York has added the likes of Shelby Harris, D.J. Reader, and Leki Fotu, but the interior of its defensive front figures to be a 2026 liability. West Virginia is not going to be a vacation trip John Harbaugh practices are not for the faint of heart 😅 @judybattista | @JamieErdahl | @Giants pic.twitter.com/42UeQDkyJY — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) July 27, 2026 These are Giants’ biggest questions entering John Harbaugh’s first training camp | NJ.com How will Giants handle the camp grind? Harbaugh is going to run a much tougher camp than Brian Daboll. That much we knew from the moment the Giants hired Harbaugh. How much of a grind will it be? Well, the Giants practice four straight days to open camp. Then they have an off day. Then they practice six straight days before their next off day. Will this help push the Giants into elite game shape? Or cause injuries? Ranking the Giants’ 6 most indispensable players: Who can they least afford to lose? | The Athletic Defense. 1. OLB Brian Burns. Not only is Burns a top-tier pass rusher who tallied an NFC-best 16.5 sacks last season, but he’s also a highly respected veteran within the Giants locker room. Just look at the turnout of teammates who showed up for his charity softball game this spring. So yes, he might be part of one of the best position rooms on the team, which hurts his case for being the most indispensable, but his presence as the face of the defense — especially with Dexter Lawrence out of town — isn’t as easily replaceable. PFF Tackle Rankings: The top 32 players ahead of the 2026 NFL season | PFF 7. Andrew Thomas, New York Giants. When healthy, Thomas is one of the top blindside protectors in the NFL. The primary issue is that he has eclipsed 900 snaps just once in the past five seasons. However, in his 13 games played in 2025, Thomas tied for fourth place among qualified tackles with a 90.3 PFF grade. He allowed just 13 total pressures, including one sack, while posting a career-high 84.5 PFF run-blocking grade. A consistently healthy Thomas gives the Giants their best chance to compete in a tough NFC East. All-Under-25 Team: Drake Maye, Abdul Carter among NFL’s ascending young players entering 2026 season | NFL.com Edge, Abdul Carter, Age 22. Carter arrived with great expectations as a top-three pick and attracted attention for his winding journey toward selecting a jersey number, then seemed to fly under the national radar throughout most of his rookie season. Those paying closer attention, however, understood that Carter had a strong debut campaign. Despite recording just four sacks in 2025, Carter finished seventh in quarterback pressures with 72 (per NGS), just five fewer than Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett recorded. He earned enough Defensive Rookie of the Year votes to finish fifth, and if he can convert more of his pressures into sacks, he’ll quickly climb the popularity charts. He turns 23 in October, too, so he has plenty of time to do so. Sisi Mauigoa on getting ready for his first camp . @NikiLattarulo talks with Giants first-rounder Francis Mauigoa at Citi Field about his first training camp and working with Jaxson Dart ➡️ @Honda pic.twitter.com/qf6rCTTDZM — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) July 26, 2026 NFL training camp storylines: Aaron Donald watch, QB battles, rookie breakouts among NFC questions | CBSSports.com How good does Malik Nabers look coming off a torn ACL? The New York Giants need Pro Bowl wide receiver Malik Nabers healthy in order to maximize 2025 first-round pick quarterback Jaxson Dart’s development. Nabers is far and away the most important developing story at Giants training camp. Nabers’ torn ACL injury wasn’t cut and dry. It also included a full meniscus repair and an extra procedure to remove inflamed scar tissue. However, New York did not place Nabers on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to begin training camp, which provided some hope that he might be ready to roll for Week 1. When he’s on the field, he’s dangerous: Nabers’ 127 career receptions through 19 career games rank as the second-most in NFL history behind only his Giants teammate Odell Beckham Jr.’s 133. New York needs Nabers to be back at full strength, and how he looks in training camp will be far and away the most important development for the Giants. summary: Through the summer, we will be counting down the Jets roster player by player. We continue the series by discussing Anez Cooper. Name: Anez Cooper Number: 72 Year With Jets: 1st Projected Role: Developmental guard His 2025: Cooper started at right guard in all 16 games for the national runner up Miami Hurricanes and earned Second Team All-ACC honors. The […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - MARCH 01: Anez Cooper of the Miami (FL) Hurricanes participates in a drill during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on March 01, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through the summer, we will be counting down the Jets roster player by player. We continue the series by discussing Anez Cooper. Name: Anez Cooper Number: 72 Year With Jets: 1st Projected Role: Developmental guard His 2025: Cooper started at right guard in all 16 games for the national runner up Miami Hurricanes and earned Second Team All-ACC honors. The Jets picked him in the sixth round of the NFL Draft. 2026 will be a success if: Cooper has a quality developmental season on the practice field and looks primed to take over the starting left guard spot in 2027. There are certain positions where you frequently see good teams find and develop late round gems. Guard is one of them. If the Jets are able to use this season turning Cooper into a starting caliber player, they will be able to save $5 million in a year moving on from Dylan Parham. Little moves like those are what make successful franchises successful. Of course the odds are against any individual late round pick from hitting, but if the Jets are going to turn it around they need more than just a few extra early picks and excess cap space. They will need to start developing late round pick like Cooper into legitimate players. Odds of making the roster: Most Likely (76-99%)

title: Eagles News: Jalen Carter contract extension draws praise
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jalen Carter and the Eagles struck a deal. What’s next for the franchise and NFL’s highest-paid DT? – The AthleticBerman: This was a smart move for the Eagles. Carter is a premium player — a true blue-chip talent with the upside to be the defensive […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 23: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles works against Cooper Beebe #56 of the Dallas Cowboys during a game at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jalen Carter and the Eagles struck a deal. What’s next for the franchise and NFL’s highest-paid DT? – The Athletic Berman: This was a smart move for the Eagles. Carter is a premium player — a true blue-chip talent with the upside to be the defensive player of the year, and those players are hard to find. He’s a building block for the Eagles. It’s a steep price, but it wasn’t going to go down. I was surprised that it stretched this far, but it was still his first offseason as an offseason-eligible player for a new deal. That’s how the Eagles have operated with their foundational players drafted in recent years, from Jalen Hurts to DeVonta Smith to Landon Dickerson to Cam Jurgens. His influence on the defense cannot be measured by his statistics. When Carter is at his best, he can change a game. (Sean McVay might have another Super Bowl if not for the way Carter played against the Rams on the final drive in the NFC divisional round playoff game in 2025.) The Eagles can and should expect more from him — whether it’s consistency or maturity — and my guess is that was part of the calculation in the investment. It’s incumbent upon Carter to understand as much. The Eagles made clear how much they valued him with this record-breaking deal. Carter is one of the best players in the league. The Eagles were smart to be aggressive. Jalen Carter Extended – Iggles Blitz Carter’s best football is ahead of him, which is good news for the Eagles and bad news for the guys who have to block him. He’s still putting all the pieces together. If he stays healthy this season, he could have a breakout year. There is the possibility that the money will have a negative effect on him, but I think playing for Clint Hurtt and Vic Fangio will be enough to keep him on the right path. At his best, this is a guy you want in the middle of your defense. Jalen Carter, Eagles agree to record-breaking contract extension – BGN Jalen Carter will neither be holding out nor holding in for a new contract this summer. With Philadelphia Eagles players reporting to the Jefferson Health Training Complex for training camp on Tuesday, the team officially announced they’ve reached a new deal with their two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle. Carter and the Eagles have reportedly agreed to a four-year, $152 million extension that could end up being worth $160 million, including $106 million guaranteed. This keeps the defensive tackle in Philly through 2031, right alongside Jordan Davis — who signed his own three-year, $78 million extension earlier this offseason. With Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis signing long-term deals with the Eagles, who’s next? – PhillyVoice Likely gone next offseason: iDL Moro Ojomo. During training camp, Ojomo was by far the top “stock up” vote getter in our annual “stock up / stock down” training camp media poll. And sure enough, he had a breakout season, collecting 38 tackles, six sacks, and 12 QB hits while playing 66 percent of the team’s defensive snaps. The Eagles were hopeful that he could capably fill in for Milton Williams, who had departed in free agency last offseason, and Ojomo delivered. JimmyVerdict: The Eagles would undoubtedly love to keep Ojomo, but after signing Carter and Davis to massive long-term deals — and the aforementioned deals for Mitchell, DeJean, and Hunt on the horizon — it’s going to be hard for the Eagles to afford him. The very obvious play from Ojomo’s camp is to wait until free agency next offseason, and cash in, like Williams did. Enjoy Moro for one last season. Eagles training camp preview: Reacting to Jalen Carter’s extension, previewing top position battles – PHLY Player I’ll be watching on Day 1, offense edition: Makai Lemon. Makai Lemon seems to be ready for camp after being sidelined with a hamstring injury during spring workouts, setting up a pivotal few weeks for the first-round rookie to acclimate to Mannion’s system and build a rapport with Jalen Hurts. He’s the type of player who should look good in training camp, so there’s reason for cautious optimism there. The Eagles need him to look good, too. Of the options at receiver around him, there isn’t one that projects as cleanly into the No. 2 role behind Smith as a featured member of the passing game and possibly the third-highest target getter behind Dallas Goedert. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has been bullish on Dontayvion Wicks since the team traded for the 25-year-old, but projecting him into the No. 2 receiver spot is, well, a projection. Smith was second on the team with 113 targets last year and Goedert had the third-highest total at 82. Wicks’ most prolific season was two years ago, when he had 76 targets, 39 catches, and 415 receiving yards. Even more staggering, Wicks’ catch rate that year was just 51.3% compared to Smith’s 68.1% and Goedert’s 73.2%. Wicks caught 65.2% of his 46 targets last season, though, and the Eagles will be banking on that upward trend continuing. Hollywood Brown’s career history has more evidence of him being capable of handling heavy usage, although his numbers have been trending down some in recent years. He’s had triple-digit targets in four consecutive seasons between 2020-2023, but would probably be better suited as a horizontal/vertical stretch role player for this receiving corps rather than a true mainstay at the top of the depth chart. For that reason, it’ll likely come down mostly to whether Lemon can hit the ground running this summer. NFL position battles in 2026: Picks to win 12 notable training camp competitions – NFL.com EDGE RUSHER OPPOSITE JONATHAN GREENARD: Jalyx Hunt vs. Nolan Smith Jr. Given how many defensive backs and defensive linemen teams rotate onto the field, there are not a ton of camp battles of consequence on defense. Even if a player doesn’t earn a starting gig, he’ll likely play a significant role. That’s true in Philly, but I wanted to highlight the edge battle between Hunt and Smith. The trade for Greenard underscored the Eagles’ need at pass rusher. Smith was pivotal during the Super Bowl run of 2024, but the triceps injury suffered in the Lombardi-lifting game seemed to take some of his bite away last season. Will he return to form? Hunt flashed upside while getting more reps in 2025, and feels like a smoother fit in Vic Fangio’s defense. Hunt has the upside to take his game to an even higher level after leading the club with 6.5 sacks last season. The outcome of this battle could play a big role in deciding which player gets paid to stay in Philly long-term. THE PICK: Hunt. Did he already break out or is there another level for the third-year pro to hit? I’m buying the latter. The six biggest roster battles as Eagles training camp gets underway – Inquirer Safety: Will Marcus Epps hold off the field? It’s worth starting with safety because it’s one of the few spots on the field where a starter is written in pencil and not pen. If you’ve been paying any attention to the Eagles since the spring, you know that Cooper DeJean is slated to move from nickel to safety in base defense. But the Eagles, like most NFL defenses, use nickel and dime packages much more often than base. So the spot next to Andrew Mukuba mostly will be manned by someone not named DeJean. Vic Fangio indicated that Marcus Epps is in the pole position for the job to replace Reed Blankenship, but the 30-year-old will have to earn it. There will be competition from converted nickel Michael Carter II, seventh-round pick Cole Wisniewski, veteran special teamer J.T. Gray, and long shots like Andre’ Sam, Kapena Gushiken, and Maximus Pulley. Don’t count out another roster addition, too, if Howie Roseman decides the Eagles need to upgrade the safety spot.…

full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 28: Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles talks trash to Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first quarter in the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has changed their roll-out of the Top 100 list, as voted by players, and it took several weeks before an Eagles player was named to the 2026 iteration. Quarterback Jalen Hurts was the lowest ranked player from Philly, coming in at No. 56, followed by CB Quinyon Mitchell at No. 47. There are still several Eagles expected to be revealed over the next few weeks, including guys like Cooper DeJean, Jalen Carter, and Saquon Barkley. The rest of the list will continue to be revealed two players per day, Monday through Friday, and then one player per day beginning Monday, August 24 through Friday, September 4. Here’s where the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles landed among the Top 100 according to their peers: No. 47: Quinyon Mitchell , CB Coming off his second season, Mitchell earned All-Pro and was immediately recognized as one of the best corners in the league. He finished the 2025 season with 17 pass breakups, allowed just 39 completions, and allowed only 94 total yards after the catch all season. The expectations for his third season have only grown, but there’s no doubt he’s capable of rising to the occasion. ESPN’s Top 100 list, as voted on by coaches and executives, knocked Mitchell for his lack of interceptions up to this point in his career, but Mitchell is consistently and reliably doing his job and locking down the best receivers in the game — his peers, at least, seem to recognize how dominant he is. No. 47 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/bOQbShgDrv — NFL (@NFL) July 28, 2026 No. 56: Jalen Hurts, QB The former Super Bowl MVP dropped a bit in this year’s list, but still ranked higher than Lamar Jackson (No. 69), Jordan Love (No. 72), and Baker Mayfield (No. 77). Hurts has a lot on his shoulders this season as the Eagles embrace a new OC and scheme, but he has done nothing but prove time-after-time that he’s up for any challenge. He’s certainly spent the offseason focused on building a solid foundation with his offensive teammates, and every indication is he’s ready for another big season. NFL’s Jeremy Bergman explains Hurts’ ranking : “Hurts threw for a career-high 25 touchdowns and rushed for eight more en route to a third Pro Bowl bid in four years. The QB’s decreased completion percentage and use in the run game likely contributed to his 37-spot drop in this year’s list, his lowest ranking since before his 2023 debut at No. 3. But Hurts remains one of the NFL’s top dual-threat signal-callers entering his seventh NFL season, with or without the departed A.J. Brown.“ No. 56 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles QB Jalen Hurts! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/vkX3kqTfSI — NFL (@NFL) July 22, 2026 Former Eagles on the list: No. 61 — CB Kevin Byard (Patriots) No. 78 — LB Josh Sweat (Cardinals) No. 80 — WR A.J. Brown (Patriots)

title: Jalen Carter, Eagles agree to record-breaking contract extension
summary: Jalen Carter will neither be holding out nor holding in for a new contract this summer. With Philadelphia Eagles players reporting to the Jefferson Health Training Complex for training camp on Tuesday, the team officially announced they’ve reached a new deal with their two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle. Carter and the Eagles have reportedly agreed […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 7: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the Cincinnati Bengals in the second half of the NFL Preseason 2025 game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 7, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Bengals 34-27. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jalen Carter will neither be holding out nor holding in for a new contract this summer. With Philadelphia Eagles players reporting to the Jefferson Health Training Complex for training camp on Tuesday, the team officially announced they’ve reached a new deal with their two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle. Carter and the Eagles have reportedly agreed to a four-year, $152 million extension that could end up being worth $160 million, including $106 million guaranteed. This keeps the defensive tackle in Philly through 2031, right alongside Jordan Davis — who signed his own three-year, $78 million extension earlier this offseason . JC is here to stay! We have agreed to terms with Jalen Carter on a contract extension through 2031. pic.twitter.com/qGlKwqJQn4 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) July 28, 2026 An annual value of $38 million makes Carter the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history. The recently extended Jeffrey Simmons ranks below him at $35.3 million per year. $38 million also puts Carter right between the annual values of Myles Garrett at $40 million and Maxx Crosby at $35.5 million. Those are the sixth-most and seventh-most valuable edge rushers, respectively. Carter has flashed immense potential since the Eagles traded up to select him with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. He was incredibly instrumental to the team’s Super Bowl success in 2024, including his late-game heroics in a playoff win over the Los Angeles Rams. Carter’s massive workload from that season seemingly left him worse off for 2025, however, as he ultimately needed a procedure on both of his shoulders . One would imagine the Eagles are extending Carter with confidence in his medical situation moving forward. Of course, it’s notable that this extension didn’t seem to be quite the “get way out of ahead of the market” aim that the Eagles typically strive for. Whether that was related to concern about his medical, his behavior (such as when he spit on Dak Prescott and missed the entire Week 1 game last year), or his consistency moving forward is not perfectly clear. But it’s also moot now in terms of their commitment to Carter. Now we’ll see if he lives up to the massive investment that the Eagles are making in him.

title: Eagles Film Review: This is a huge offseason for Ty Robinson
summary: One of my favorite things to do every offseason is to go back and compare my post-draft notes on the Eagles’ rookies with how they actually looked when they got on the field. It’s a fun blend of film study, self-evaluation, and a check on how well certain traits really translate to the NFL. I […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 5: Ty Robinson #95 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Denver Broncos at Lincoln Financial Field on October 5, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of my favorite things to do every offseason is to go back and compare my post-draft notes on the Eagles’ rookies with how they actually looked when they got on the field. It’s a fun blend of film study, self-evaluation, and a check on how well certain traits really translate to the NFL. I won’t be writing full scouting reports here, as I did that after the draft. This series is more about reviewing last year’s film in comparison to my pre-draft thoughts. Did the player perform as expected? Did anything surprise me? And what do I think comes next? At the end of each article, I’ll give my updated outlook for that player in the future. Previously: Jihaad Campbell / Andrew Mukuba Ty Robinson Ty Robinson was probably the Eagles draft pick I was least excited about on draft weekend. Not because I disliked the player, but because I had watched 15 defensive tackles before the draft, and Robinson was the 16th on my list to watch. Sigh. After getting over the initial disappointment, Robinson became one of my favorite players to study. “he’s the most fun player I’ve watched that the Eagles drafted and he plays like a wrecking ball.” His effort level jumped off the screen at Nebraska, and although I wasn’t convinced he had the physical tools to become a star, I thought the Eagles had drafted someone who could carve out an immediate role in their defensive line rotation. Looking back now, that looks incredibly optimistic. I wasn’t projecting Robinson to become the next Moro Ojomo or Milton Williams. “I’m not sure he has the physical traits ever to become a high-level starter” Robinson was already 24 years old as a rookie, which is exactly why I believed he’d contribute immediately. Older prospects are usually more physically and mentally prepared for the NFL than younger developmental players, and I felt Robinson’s experience would allow him to play meaningful snaps from Day One. “I feel pretty convinced that he will have a role as a rookie and contribute immediately” I expected a dependable rotational defensive tackle who could defend the run on early downs, provide the occasional interior pass rush, and give the Eagles solid, unspectacular football. Most of the weaknesses I highlighted before the draft ended up appearing during Robinson’s rookie season. What I completely misjudged was how much those weaknesses would limit him early in his career. I thought Robinson’s strengths would outweigh the flaws enough for him to become a useful rotational player straight away. Instead, they prevented him from earning Vic Fangio’s trust at all. Things I Expected My expectations for Robinson were never particularly ambitious. I expected a reliable fourth defensive tackle who could play 20 to 30 snaps a game and allow the Eagles to keep their stars fresh. However, looking back at my report, the weaknesses I saw on film were the same ones we saw last year. In my weakness section from last year, I mentioned all of this… “he doesn’t always show quickness or explosiveness in games despite very good testing numbers” “he can play too upright” “he lacks a counter when his go-to move (the club) doesn’t work” “he ends up on the ground a little too often.” Those concerns were everywhere on film last year. He didn’t look explosive. He was far too upright against the run, and had no counter when his club move didn’t work. His club move did work once or twice, but he had nothing when offensive linemen knew that was coming. There was not much else about his rookie season that I saw coming. In hindsight, I wasn’t wrong about his strengths and weaknesses, but I was wrong about how it would translate. He did flash a few of the traits that I liked in college, such as a strong club move once or twice, and he made a couple of plays against the run that reminded me of Ty Robinson from college, but there wasn’t much else. 6) Hey, I thought Ty Robinson made some plays against the run! He's obviously had a very disappointing rookie season, but he showed some flashes in this game as a run defender. Which is something, at least! pic.twitter.com/qswCGdgLuc — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) January 6, 2026 And even when we see him win vs outside zone, which was something he was outstanding at in college, he still couldn’t finish and make the tackle. This has to be better. His real strength was moving laterally and winning against outside runs. The Good: Seeing Ty Robinson move laterally to win vs OZ, which was a big strength of his coming out. The Bad: The tackle. Yikes. pic.twitter.com/XKByhshaLL — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) July 20, 2026 Things That Surprised Me The biggest surprise wasn’t just Robinson’s lack of playing time. The Eagles had one of the deepest defensive line rotations in football. What surprised me was how he looked when he actually got on the field. The film was bad. Robinson turned 25 during his second offseason and was older than Moro Ojomo despite Ojomo already entering his fourth NFL season. Normally, older interior defensive linemen are viewed as players with lower ceilings but higher floors. They may never become stars, but they’re often ready to contribute much sooner than younger prospects. Robinson finished his rookie season with just 104 defensive snaps, and 51 of those came in Week 18 after the Eagles rested their starters. Strip that game away, and he played just 53 meaningful defensive snaps all season. For a player I expected to have one of the highest floors in the class, that’s a bad outcome. It wasn’t just that Robinson failed to become an important rotational player. He barely became part of the rotation at all. That’s where my evaluation missed the mark. I believed Robinson’s age and experience made him one of the safest projections in the Eagles’ draft class. Instead, his rookie season suggested he was much further away from contributing than I ever anticipated. I expected Robinson to arrive as a relatively polished player. I was wrong. The biggest concern was his run defense. There were too many snaps where he struggled simply to hold his ground. Double teams gave him real problems, which isn’t unusual for an undersized interior defensive lineman listed at 6-foot-5 and 288 pounds. More worrying were the snaps where he lost against single blockers. Robinson played too upright, lost leverage far too easily, and was moved off the ball much more frequently than I anticipated. His pass rushing wasn’t much better. Early in the season, Robinson beat Jon Runyan Jr. with an impressive club move that immediately caught my attention. This was what he did in college! 3) The coverage here is excellent, and it leaves Dart with nowhere to go. Sadly, the rush lane integrity is poor, and Zack Baun takes a bad angle and is beaten in space. It looks bad for Baun, but these tackles, where you are isolated in space, can be hard to make. It was great… pic.twitter.com/TFjHtuGKKx — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2025 Robinson relied heavily on that same club move throughout the season, and once offensive linemen handled it, there was very little else to threaten them. If his first move failed, the rep was usually over. There was little evidence of a developed counter move or a clear pass-rush plan. The most surprising thing, though, was how different Robinson looked compared to the player I watched at Nebraska. In college, he played like a wrecking ball. He was relentless, violent, and constantly around the football. His film was hilarious at times. That version of Robinson rarely appeared as a rookie. Would describe new #Eagles DT Ty Robinson a bull in a china shop. Physical, heavy hands, no nonsense pass rushers, used in multiple alignments along the Nebraska defensive line. pic.twitter.com/f0yJU2ujIq — Devin Jackson (@RealD_Jackson)…

title: Eagles News: Darius Cooper among training camp trade candidates
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Five Eagles players on the trade block heading into training camp – PhillyVoiceWR Darius Cooper. Cooper had a great camp and an encouraging preseason showing as an undrafted rookie receiver out of Tarleton State last season. He made the 53-man roster and managed to stay […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 04: Darius Cooper #80 of the Philadelphia Eagles kneels before the NFL 2025 game between Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on September 04, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Five Eagles players on the trade block heading into training camp – PhillyVoice WR Darius Cooper. Cooper had a great camp and an encouraging preseason showing as an undrafted rookie receiver out of Tarleton State last season. He made the 53-man roster and managed to stay on it the entire season, appearing in 13 games. He made 9 receptions for 92 yards on 11 targets, while playing something of a “dirty work” role in the Eagles offense after Johnny Wilson was lost for the season with an injury. Although the Eagles’ starting receivers may not be as strong on paper as they were a year ago when A.J. Brown was on the roster, they do have better depth with the additions of first-round pick Makai Lemon, trade acquisition Dontayvion Wicks, and free agent signing Hollywood Brown. Wilson is also back, and he had a good spring. Cooper could make more sense for a non-contending team willing to use a roster spot on a young prospect with traits that can be developed. Projected cost: Some other back-of-the-roster depth guy at a position of need. Makai Lemon is a versatile player – BGN Former Eagles undrafted free agent Reed Blankenship earned a huge new contract with the Houston Texans this offseason, and he and Cooper DeJean welcomed Blankenship’s new teammate Calen Bullock on their Exciting Mics podcast. Bullock overlapped with Makai Lemon for one year at USC and he recalled when the Eagles’ rookie wide receiver actually played in games at cornerback. Bullock explained that a lot of their corners were hurt that season, and Lemon played both receiver and corner in high school, so they had to call him over to play on defense. The WR took 18 defensive snaps (per Pro Football Focus) his rookie season in 2023, but eventually made his way back to the offensive side of the ball. Eagles training camp: Storylines, position battles, concerns and potential trades – The Athletic Kubena: Roseman should continue fielding calls on Jalen Carter. As Zach said, he has the talent to be one of the best defensive players in the NFL. His value as a 25-year-old with two years left on his rookie deal should be very, very high. The Eagles aren’t ready to commit long-term to a player, however dominant, who was ejected in Week 1 last year for spitting on Dak Prescott, dealt with nagging shoulder issues that required medical attention, and experienced an overall dip in his game. Other teams have expressed their interest in Carter in the past. The Eagles should get at least one first-round pick in such a deal. Could they get two? Or something close? And which player(s) could they trade for by pairing that haul with the 2028 first-round pick they received for Brown? 2026 NFL offseason: Top impact signings, trades, draft picks – ESPN Riq Woolen, CB (signed by Philadelphia Eagles). One of the most underrated signings in free agency, Woolen fits well on the perimeter of Vic Fangio’s defense. Woolen can align opposite Quinyon Mitchell, giving the Eagles two long cover corners who can open and run. (Meanwhile, Cooper DeJean can play the slot in nickel sets.) Woolen allowed 5.0 yards per target in coverage last season, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, which ranked fourth best among the 87 defensive backs who were targeted at least 50 times. […] Makai Lemon, WR (drafted by Philadelphia Eagles) With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon steps into the No. 2 role opposite DeVonta Smith under new coordinator Sean Mannion. Lemon has the route traits and foot quickness to manipulate coverage, and he can accelerate through the ball to create easy yards after the catch. He is willing to work the heavy traffic areas of the field, which should lead to targets in Mannion’s system — one that should use more three-step and play-action concepts than previous seasons in Philly. Everything you need to know as Eagles begin 2026 training camp – NBCSP A bunch of changes on offense. The Eagles were far too talented last season to finish with the NFL’s No. 24-ranked offense. So after the season, they moved on from Kevin Patullo and launched an exhaustive offensive coordinator search that eventually led them to Sean Mannion. The former NFL backup quarterback has been coaching for just two seasons but the Eagles are excited about his potential with a Shanahan-style scheme he’s bringing to Philly. This offense will look very different in 2026 than what we have seen in the first five years under head coach Nick Sirianni. The Eagles enter training camp with a number of intriguing storylines. We ranked their importance. – Inquirer Jalen Hurts. Was there an NFL player under a bigger microscope than Hurts this offseason? Between the ESPN report that detailed friction concerning Hurts, the A.J. Brown saga, the constant debates over his standing among NFL quarterbacks, Hurts dominated headlines all offseason. So can he block out that noise and silence his doubters with a strong camp? It’d be easy to say “yes” and just move on, but the reality is that Hurts is at a crossroads. He’s learning another new offense and it’s drastically different from the last one he ran. His new OC gushed about him in his first news conference, but can that honeymoon phase survive a weak training camp/slow start to the season? That’s not to mention the fact that Hurts has a handful of unproven new weapons trying to replace a No. 1 wide receiver in Brown. How Hurts deals with these hurdles is easily the most intriguing camp storyline. His future in Philadelphia will be in question all season. He can quell some of that noise with a decent July and August. All-Under-25 Team: Drake Maye, Abdul Carter among NFL’s ascending young players entering 2026 season – NFL.com COOPER DEJEAN — We should have known DeJean was on track to produce a special 2025 campaign when he intercepted Patrick Mahomes and returned it for a touchdown in Super Bowl LIX. His first career pick in the final game of his rookie season was a preview of what was to come in a splashy Year 2. After securing a Lombardi Trophy to close the 2024 season, DeJean saw his role increase in 2025 and matched the expectation, tallying 16 passes defensed, two interceptions, 93 tackles and a -12.1 target EPA in 580 coverage snaps, per Next Gen Stats. Inserted at slot corner, DeJean formed one half of Philadelphia’s first-team All-Pro defensive back pair with Quinyon Mitchell, taking home the prestigious honor (plus a Pro Bowl nod) while playing an integral role in the Eagles’ eighth-ranked pass defense. He’s only 23, yet he’s already proven himself as an elite nickelback with plenty of road left in front of him. Former Eagles head coach hired to call college football games – PennLive Former Philadelphia Eagles head coach Doug Pederson, who led the franchise to a win in Super Bowl LII, will work as a college football analyst in 2026. Pederson has been hired by CBS Sports, the network announced Monday. Cowboys offseason surprisingly drama free, enter training camp more focused – Blogging The Boys When it comes to the Dallas Cowboys, it seems as if the organization corners the market on drama every offseason. This team is continuously on the lips of the media every year and it’s no wonder with an owner like Jerry Jones, who loves/craves the headline-grabbing free publicity. That’s why it’s so surprising things have been so quiet and drama free this offseason. The Dallas Cowboys report to Oxnard, California this week to kick off training camp with zero headline-grabbing stories. This hasn’t been the case in the past. Usually at this time entering training camp the Cowboys are still facing the never-ending contract negotiations with one player or another. In…

title: Browns complicate Steelers’ contract negotiations with Joey Porter Jr

title: T.J. Watt shares promising insight into Steelers’ pass rush plan
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers could have a much more versatile look on defense in 2026. Speaking on Tuesday at the first day of training camp, star linebacker T.J. Watt said fans should expect to see not only himself, but fellow edge rushers Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig lining up at multiple spots across the defensive front […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 23: T.J. Watt #90 of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 23, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers could have a much more versatile look on defense in 2026. Speaking on Tuesday at the first day of training camp, star linebacker T.J. Watt said fans should expect to see not only himself, but fellow edge rushers Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig lining up at multiple spots across the defensive front rather than staying in traditional roles. “I know I say it every year, but I truly mean it,” Watt said . “We all are going to be moving around.” The comments offer another glimpse into what new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham is building. Known for deploying creative fronts and disguising pressure packages throughout his coaching career, Graham appears intent on maximizing the Steelers’ trio of premier pass rushers by creating favorable matchups and making it more difficult for opposing offenses to identify where pressure is coming from. While Watt has primarily rushed from the left side and Highsmith from the right during their time together, both have shown the ability to switch sides when needed. Herbig has also emerged as an explosive rotational pass rusher, earning a larger role after flashing his ability to pressure quarterbacks in limited opportunities. If Graham follows through on that philosophy, Pittsburgh’s defense could become significantly less predictable, with Watt, Highsmith, and Herbig attacking from different alignments both on the edge and potentially inside on passing downs. For a Steelers defense built around generating pressure without excessive blitzing, the increased movement could be one of the defining wrinkles of the 2026 season. full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JUNE 11: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on June 11, 2026 in Renton, Washington. Unlike Monday’s session, which was limited to credentialed media only, this was another public practice in front of a full house at Virginia Mason Athletic Center in Renton. They’re still not in pads yet, but come Thursday things will really start to ramp up in terms of intensity and what’s allowed in camp. Here’s a recap of notable events from Day 4. Seahawks training camp news and notes A big day for Jalen Milroe Maybe the Seahawks will post some highlights, but otherwise Seattle is restrictive as far as training camp video. It’s been a purportedly tough start to camp for Milroe, but the splash plays came in bunches for the former Alabama quarterback. I’ll just let some friends of Field Gulls and Tacoma News Tribune’s Gregg Ball do the talking. Milroe is breaking the pocket often when pressured, but doing a great job of a young Russ Wilson impression by constantly looking downfield and finding the open man for a completion — Chickens and Mentals Caretaker (@_danchu) July 29, 2026 Another Milroe play action right scramble left to Ricky white And now Milroe lofts a 30 yard beauty over prices shoulder for a score #seahawks https://t.co/d9JtnpqdXZ — Curtis Allen (@curtis93969) July 28, 2026 QB Jalen Milroe signing for fans after his best throwing day in his two NFL training camps with the #Seahawks Dart throw into Cody White’s chest back of end zone. Throw across his body in stride to TE Eric Saubert over the middle. Zipped 2 more outside throws in tight coverage pic.twitter.com/Hihpnniy5l — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) July 28, 2026 The only bad news for Milroe was getting pick 6’d on a tip ball that landed in rookie safety Bud Clark’s hands, but is it bad news if the recipient is a ball-hawking rookie safety? And apparently Clark did the Marshawn Lynch backsplash/crotch grab touchdown celebration for good measure. Rylie Mills, healthy and whole The former Notre Dame defensive end missed most of his rookie season after tearing his ACL during the College Football Playoff. He came back in time for spot duties late in the regular season, then sacked Drake Maye in the Super Bowl. With a full offseason in Mike Macdonald’s system, Mills is poised for a lot more involvement on defense. Now… what if we got to see him be a special teams gunner? How athletic is defensive end Rylie Mills? How healthy is he after missing as a rookie last year into December following reconstructive knee surgery? #Seahawks , coach Jay Harbaugh have him running down as a gunner in special-teams drills in training camp @thenewstribune pic.twitter.com/7Jzs3aV1u2 — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) July 28, 2026 Rookie cornerback Julian Neal among those not practicing It’s time to worry when it’s time to worry, but it’s worth keeping an eye out on a few non-participants over the next few days. Julian Neal left Monday’s practice early, as did Jake Bobo, and both were held out of Tuesday’s session. “We had a couple guys today that we took in,” Mike Macdonald said on Monday. “Didn’t seem like anything major, but we’re going to get him checked out. See what we need to do.” Some notes from Seahawks practice today… DNPs: Julian Neal, Jamie Sheriff, Josh Jones, Jake Bobo, Jarran Reed. Jalen Milroe has had some rough days, but this wasn't one of them. Maybe his best practice I've seen with Seattle. A few really nice throws. — Curtis Crabtree (@Curtis_Crabtree) July 28, 2026 Neal had been practicing with the second-team defense. Noah Igbinoghene and Nehemiah Pritchett got some extra work in his absence. Special teamer Irv Charles also did not practice after picking up a knock earlier in the week. Leonard Williams reveals what’s different about Brian Fleury’s offense With Klint Kubiak coaching the Las Vegas Raiders, the Seahawks are once again learning a new offense. Unlike Ryan Grubb to Kubiak, the transition from Kubiak to new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury should be smoother. Fleury is expected to run a lot of Kubiak’s offense but add his own flavoring, which based on Leonard Williams’ observations, should feature more motion. “Yeah, there’s a lot more motion,” Williams said. “Fullback motion, tight end motions. Sometimes the tight end is in a fullback position and vice versa. It’s definitely keeping our defense on our toes, and they’re switching it up a lot. Sometimes they’ll motion two tight ends to one side, and they’ll run the ball that way. Sometimes they’ll motion two to one side and run the ball the opposite way. So, you can’t really guess, you’ve got to really just read your keys.” Highlight of the Day: Jadarian Price continues to get work in the passing game First-round draft pick Jadarian Price doesn’t have much history as a receiving back. He had just 15 career grabs at Notre Dame, but that doesn’t mean he’s not going to be a threat in the pros. On Monday, he beat Ernest Jones on a wheel route for a touchdown. Same route, different player (Maxen Hook), same result. Rook's got hands. @Jadarian15 pic.twitter.com/OyuVIQvGOJ — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) July 29, 2026 Ernest Jones said this of Price after Monday’s practice: “He’s good. He’s good, man. Mature for his age. You don’t get too many words out of him, but he’s working. He got me today. He had a hell of a route on me today. He’s good. I think he’s going to help us. He’s doing everything right and he’s got a great group of backs in front of him that are kind of teaching him the way.” Wednesday is a day off for the players before returning to the practice field on Thursday. full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 30: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 and Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks jog onto the field in the first quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings at Lumen Field on November 30, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks will be throwing it back to the 1990s for two of their nine home games this regular season . Seattle’s widely acclaimed throwback uniforms will be worn in primetime against a pair of high profile opponents: Week 7 (Oct. 25) vs. Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football Week 13 (Dec. 7) vs. Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football The Seahawks are permitted up to three throwback games under the NFL’s alternate uniform policy. Last year they had an iconic double throwback thriller with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who were also celebrating their 50th season and came out of Lumen Field as 38-35 winners. Seattle took its throwbacks on the road to Maryland for a 38-14 beatdown of the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football, before scoring a 26-0 shoutout win in the same unis against the Minnesota Vikings. Seattle introduced the 1990s-inspired throwbacks in the 2023 season, winning 24-20 over the Cleveland Browns . The first road game throwbacks came against the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football , with Dallas taking a 41-35 shootout. The Seahawks opened the Mike Macdonald era donning throwbacks in their 26-20 victory over the Denver Broncos, but had a rough one on Thursday Night Football against the San Francisco 49ers a few weeks later. Win or lose, look how clean these jerseys are! Who doesn’t love the silver helmets? In other Seahawks news, the “Rivalries” uniforms the Seahawks debuted in their classic 38-37 overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams last season will return for their Christmas Day primetime outing against the Rams. It looks as if the Action Green unis have been retired once and for all.

full_text: As the 2026 NFL season inches closer and closer, EA Sports has begun to release their Madden 27 player ratings. This started with them announcing players in the “99 club,” including reigning offensive player of the year, Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The newest batch of ratings released are for the 2026 rookies. Let’s take a look at where EA Sports has ranked the rookie class for the Seattle Seahawks . Safety, Bud Clark: 75 overall Running back, Jadarian Price: 75 overall Cornerback, Julian Neal: 71 overall Right guard, Beau Stephens: 70 overall Cornerback, Andre Fuller: 67 overall Wide receiver, Emmanuel Henderson Jr.: 67 overall Cornerback, Michael Dansby: 67 overall Defensive tackle, Deven Eastern: 64 overall The first items that come to mind when looking at these ratings is that EA Sports seems to have been less strict in their rookie ratings this season compared to previous ones. Typically rookies will receive comically low ratings. However, this season four of the eight draft picks a rating over 70 seems a little more reasonable. To add some more context to the overall rookie ratings, only four players received a rating of over 80 Dallas Cowboys safety, Caleb Downs: 82 Arizona Cardinals running back, Jeremiyah Love: 82 New York Jets right edge, David Bailey: 81 Tampa Bay Buccaneers left edge, Reuben Bain Jr.: 80 Another thing to keep an eye on when more ratings drop later is where some of the Seahawk veterans are rated, specifically in the safety and running back room. With Bud Clark and Jadarian Price receiving a 75 overall rating, will those be good enough to surpass some veterans in the room such as Zach Charbonnet or Ty Okada? What about right guard? One would think that Anthony Bradford should have a higher rating at right guard than Beau Stephens at 70. However, EA Sports has done crazier things. Another one to keep in mind is cornerback. Devon Witherspoon will surely have a higher rating than any of the rookie cornerbacks. Josh Jobe should as well. However, it will be interesting to see where the rest of the cornerback room (Nehemiah Pritchett, Noah Igbinoghene, Shemar Jean-Charles, and Brandon Johnson) end up in comparison to the rookies. Of course Madden ratings are only that. They will have no bearing on the actual camp battles the Seahawks will have (obviously). That being said, it is still fun to see where the new Seahawk players end up in a completely arbitrary set of ratings by EA Sports. Just don’t put too much weight into them ( unless you want to be like the New York Jets .)
