title: Seahawks star Byron Murphy II aiming for double-digit sacks in 2026
summary: One of the most underrated young cornerstones of the new era of Seattle Seahawks football was the very first pick (16th overall) of the new John Schneider/Mike Macdonald regime. Byron Murphy II is already accomplished after two years in the league. He sees himself as “dominant” against the run. Stats, but mostly the eye test, […]
full_text: One of the most underrated young cornerstones of the new era of Seattle Seahawks football was the very first pick (16th overall) of the new John Schneider/Mike Macdonald regime. Byron Murphy II is already accomplished after two years in the league. He sees himself as “dominant” against the run. Stats, but mostly the eye test, confirm that notion. Murphy does a lot of the dirty work on the ground. His sights, however, are set on improvement across the board, including in pass rush productivity. When discussing the run game, Murphy talks his talk, proclaiming in his interview with Seattle Sports : “I know I’m a master at it.” He then immediately pointed out the need to constantly improve, despite that feeling. "I'm trying to get double-digit sacks this year." 👀 #Seahawks DT Byron Murphy II discusses the area of his game he's worked on the most this offseason on with @WymanAndBob pic.twitter.com/xhDu6bEE4F — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) July 28, 2026 Murphy confidently reveals one of his goals for the 2026 season: “I’m mainly focused on pass rushing, though. That’s my biggest thing. I’m trying to get double digit sacks this year.” This, after a 7-sack output in ‘25. Those are strong words, but ones that are backed up by a belief. That belief is reflected in the opinions of his teammates. Edge rusher, Derick Hall ( who just got paid by the Seahawks ) was asked about Murphy II during the preseason in the leadup to an eventual championship run: “Last year I think Murph was hugely effective. He’s one of the best to play the double team in a league, I feel like that’s his strong point being able to add the scale of pass rush” … Derick went on to state how he feels that, “Byron is going to have a really, really huge year for us.” Indeed, he did. Murphy finished third in sacks among all interior defensive linemen, notching seven QB takedowns. They weren’t flukes either, with BMII ranking top ten in pressures (50). In a year in which they finished as the No. 1 scoring defense, the Seattle Seahawks stop unit held the New England Patriots to only 78 yards gained through three quarters of Super Bowl play. Per Seahawks.com : “This defense ranks No. 8, all time in DVOA defense going as far back as 1978, which is how far DVOA stats go back.” After a resounding Super Bowl win with multiple major contributions from a talent-laden “Dark Side” defense, star safety, Julian Love discussed how the defense put up such an impressive performance. Love said, “Yeah, it’s a combined effort. To be able to run the scheme that we do and have success the way we have, it just takes talent. It starts up front. Byron Murphy, honestly, is the heartbeat of our defense. And he’s just an unsung hero. I think his name needs to be mentioned more him, Leonard Williams, Jarran Reed up front, the depth that we have in the interior.” Byron Murphy talked in a previous sit-down with Wyman and Bob about “how much dedication it took” to grow into his expanded role in 2025. He went on to say, “I know I can be the best D-tackle in this league. In order to do that, I just gotta make strides, each and every day. Work on my game. Yeah man… I’m aiming high this year.” For the uninitiated, defensive guys have a whole different way about them. You love to see the nasty and the swagger out of those guys. Murphy said of the return of training camp: “I’m just happy to be here. I was ready to get back. Ready to get back to something I love doing, which is football.” Can Murphy get even better in year three? If he continues to apply that monster work ethic, that will shine through even in the middle of the trenches. He’ll need three more sacks than he recorded last year to meet one of his goals. It’ll be exciting to see how much better year three of Byron Murphy II can get, and in turn, year three of the Mike Macdonald defense in Seattle.

title: Bloomberg report says Vinod Khosla has ‘no intention of running the Seahawks’
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are in the process of finalizing the biggest franchise sale in NFL history, with the Khosla family set to purchase the Super Bowl champions for a whopping $9.612 billion. While Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla is the main name behind this ownership group, it’s already been confirmed that his wife, Neeru Khosla, […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 28: Vinod Khosla, Founder, Khosla Ventures, speaks onstage during day two of TechCrunch Disrupt 2025 at Moscone Center on October 28, 2025 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Kimberly White/Getty Images for TechCrunch) | Getty Images for TechCrunch The Seattle Seahawks are in the process of finalizing the biggest franchise sale in NFL history, with the Khosla family set to purchase the Super Bowl champions for a whopping $9.612 billion. While Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla is the main name behind this ownership group, it’s already been confirmed that his wife, Neeru Khosla, would serve as the controlling owner . In a recent Bloomberg article, which focused on Khosla Ventures’ plan to raise $5.5 billion in investment funds, of which much of it would be spent investing in startup companies, there’s a nugget regarding how Vinod sees his role in the Seahawks organization. Or, perhaps more accurately, not much of one. Recently, Khosla personally led an investor group to buy the Seattle Seahawks for $9.6 billion, a deal that if closed would be expected to set a National Football League record. On a recent fundraising call, investors were told that Khosla has no intention of running the Seahawks and is dedicated to his venture investing business, according to people familiar with the matter. Vinod and Neeru’s son, Neal Khosla, “would be expected to have a significant leadership role in the ownership group,” according to the NFL memo sent out to teams earlier this month . Neal previously interned with his hometown San Francisco 49ers back in 2014. Meanwhile, there have been questions concerning whether or not there will be other members of the ownership group outside of the Khoslas. Bloomberg additionally reported that there are , “talks with multiple parties to join the consortium, according to people familiar with the matter. “The discussions include former Sequoia Capital managing partner Mark Stevens and the private equity firm Sixth Street Partners. Carlyle Group Inc. and Dynasty Equity Partners Management are in talks regarding a joint bid,” the report added. Neither the Carlyle Group nor Dynasty Equity has ever invested in an NFL team, whereas Sixth Street Partners has a stake in the New England Patriots. Carlyle does hold a stake in the National Women’s Soccer League’s Seattle Reign. You might be wondering if private equity is subject to the same rules as everyone else in terms of not being allowed to have ownership stakes in multiple teams. That is not the case, as Bloomberg’s article notes, “NFL rules permit the league’s four approved private equity businesses to buy into as many as six clubs. The firms can own as much as 10% in a single club and have to take a 3% stake at a minimum.” The league owners will convene on Aug. 26 to ratify the sale.

The police report doesn’t say that.” Shanahan then gave his full version of the events that led up to and through the collision between his Tesla Model S and the other driver’s SUV — a crash that left Shanahan with a concussion, a broken left hand, a broken nose, three broken ribs and 40 stitches above his right eye. “I was going 20 miles an hour,” Shanahan said. “I was not on my phone, but I dropped my phone and it was stuck in my seats. It’s on my lap and it slid off. And I went down to look for it and took my eyes off the road for two seconds. And as I was coming up, the airbags hit me in my face, and they broke my nose. And then they said the visor really gashed me. … I took my eyes off the road looking for my phone, and my car veered into someone. “It’s one of those roads where there’s no forgiveness. … When I hit her, the impact was just so, I’ll just never forget how violent it was.” …..While Shanahan is healing well, he does not yet have a timeline for when he expects to return to coaching full time. He cites fatigue as one of his biggest obstacles, noting he had a good day Monday but was feeling a bit worse Tuesday. But Shanahan also wanted to clarify that while his concussion was serious, he did not have amnesia and never lost consciousness. Most of all, the coach said he wanted to make sure that someone else wasn’t getting the blame for something he did. “It just crushed me hearing the girl get blamed for it,” Shanahan said. “I’m just lucky that I survived, that she didn’t get hurt and that I didn’t lose my eye.” 49ers signing LB Quinton Bell to a one-year deal “The then-Oakland Raiders selected Bell out of Prairie View A&M in the seventh round (No. 230 overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft. summary: Having had an injury scare on the defensive line early in training camp when Romello Height was carted off with cramps, the 49ers have made a move to boost their pass rush options off the edge. Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the 49ers are signing defensive end KJ Henry after he had a workout at […]

(Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Having had an injury scare on the defensive line early in training camp when Romello Height was carted off with cramps, the 49ers have made a move to boost their pass rush options off the edge. Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the 49ers are signing defensive end KJ Henry after he had a workout at the team’s facility. Henry, a fifth-round pick of the Commanders in 2023, was most recently with the Pittsburgh Steelers in the spring having bounced around the league over his first three seasons in the league. Having tallied 13.5 sacks and 28.5 tackles for loss over a five-season career with Clemson that saw him display intriguing the lateral quickness to win to the tackle’s inside shoulder and the flexibility to bend around the edge, Henry has struggled to make those skills translate to the next level. He had 1.5 sacks in his first and only season with the Commanders and has never topped that number across spells with the Cincinnati Bengals, Dallas Cowboys and Cleveland Browns. The 49ers have previously shown interest in Henry, having had a Zoom interview with him prior to the 2023 draft. Henry’s signing means the Niners now have 10 defensive ends on the roster and he likely faces an uphill battle to make the team, with Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Height, Keion White all locks for the 53 and Sam Okuayinonu a strong bet to join them. But there is value in making low-risk bets on players experienced players that have previously displayed enticing physical gifts. If Henry shows enough across camp and preseason to land on the practice squad, this could prove to be an astute July move by San Francisco.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan clarifies the details of his accident on July 14
summary: Initial reports about San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan claimed he was not at fault for the car crash that occurred on July 14. According to the California Crash Reporting System database — Case ID 5249308 — Shanahan was allegedly holding and using his cell phone prior to the crash. Still, Shanahan was not […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 21: Head coach of the Wildcats FFC, Kyle Shanahan looks on before the Fanatics Flag Football Classic at BMO Stadium on March 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images for OBB Media - FANATICS STUDIOS) | Getty Images for OBB Media - FAN Initial reports about San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan claimed he was not at fault for the car crash that occurred on July 14. According to the California Crash Reporting System database — Case ID 5249308 — Shanahan was allegedly holding and using his cell phone prior to the crash. Still, Shanahan was not considered at fault. It was determined that the 21-year-old woman driving made an unsafe turn, which resulted in the crash. Both airbags were deployed. The state of California prohibits holding and operating a cell phone while driving, according to Vehicle Code 23123.5(a) , but Shanahan was not cited. Chris Simms said he received pictures from Kyle’s wife, Mandy. Simms said, “He was this close to maybe losing his right eye. The scar is so big right here. And he’s still battling with this concussion. He’s healing. His face looks a whole lot better, but this concussion, of course, being part of that kind of accident, is lingering, and it’s giving him issues.” Here’s more from Simms, via PFT live on Monday: “I don’t think he’d have any problem with me sharing this. It hit him hard, right? He was emotional about it, because he realized how close it was to being just a complete, you know, utter disaster. Like, really, it was a disaster anyways. But, you know, when you’re that part of that accident, like I said, he could have lost his right eye. It could have been a lot worse. You know, he’s very concerned about the woman he got in the accident with and how she is and handling that situation. So there’s just a lot there. And I think it was a lot for him to process . . . at first as well. And then, of course, with it being, you know, a few days before you’ve got to start going to the office and worrying about football and everything else on top of it, where your break’s ending and you’re dealing with that as well, yeah, it was tough for him. It’s tough for their family. Their kids were in shock, and, you know, you just realize how fragile life can be, and how it can all change in just one split second. And thank God he’s okay. But, yeah, he’s gonna have to deal with this and, you know, hopefully get his mind cleared up here over the next few weeks.” Speaking of PFT, Mike Florio continues to focus on why this story didn’t come out sooner and why Bay Area media isn’t going down a rabbit hole to find out information about the case, as opposed to Shanahan’s health. He wasn’t at fault in a serious, traumatizing accident. We are not entitled to every detail that happens with the 49ers or Shanahan. It does not matter when we get this information. The only reason we can access details about the car accident is through Shanahan’s friend, Simms, or public records. That’s more than enough. The official language for cell phone use: “A violation of this section is an infraction punishable by a base fine of twenty dollars ($20) for a first offense and fifty dollars ($50) for each subsequent offense. Let’s not pretend to act all high and mighty because Shanahan had his phone in his hand. It’s something everyone does, and you can see it if you look to your right or left when you’re driving. If the state of California felt like it was a serious offense, the penalties would be much more severe. That’s not to excuse using the phone, but the potential fines speak for themselves. Kyle’s update, 12:33 p.m. PT: Kyle Shanahan met with a few media members to clarify details from the accident. According to Matt Maiocco , Shanahan said, “I was going 20 miles an hour. I was not on my phone, but I dropped my phone, and it was stuck in my seats. It was on my lap, and it slid off, and I went down to look for it, and took my eyes off the road for two seconds, and I was coming up; the airbags hit me in my face.” Shanahan corrected reports saying that he was not at fault. Shanahan said, “I hit her. I don’t know why it was reported that way.” Apparently, this all stemmed from a clerical error in the California Crash Reporting System database that is being corrected. Shanahan continued, saying, “It just crushed me that the other driver gets blamed for it.” There’s nothing for Shanahan to hide in this situation, so good on him for coming out and stating the truth.

title: 3 Training Camp notes from 49ers Day 2 practice: There’s 1 constant at safety
summary: Day two of training camp for the San Francisco 49ers was eventful. Before the second session, the team released information on the newest 49ers injuries, as OT Vadarian Lowe will miss some time, and WR Christian Kirk and DT Gracen Holton are dealing with injuries that will limit them moving forward. RB Jordan James wasn’t […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 11: Ji'Ayir Brown #27 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Day two of training camp for the San Francisco 49ers was eventful. Before the second session, the team released information on the newest 49ers injuries, as OT Vadarian Lowe will miss some time, and WR Christian Kirk and DT Gracen Holton are dealing with injuries that will limit them moving forward. RB Jordan James wasn’t seen during the second portion of Monday’s session, but it is unclear whether it was due to an injury, and the team breathed a sigh of relief as rookie EDGE Romello Height was carted off before the official diagnosis of cramps was announced. Here are three notes from day two of 49ers training camp Stribling has a golden opportunity to gain reps Even before Kirk’s injury, it felt as if the 49ers were pushing rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling into the third receiver role, at the very least. Now, with Kirk set to miss valuable practice time, Stribling has a chance to put a stranglehold on his role with very little competition. Stribling, in addition to Mike Evans and Ricky Pearsall, has a chance to be explosive, as Stribling can move all over the field and can flip positions with Pearsall. Brock Purdy praised Stribling in his press conference following the session on Monday. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner writes: “Purdy has been impressed by the early returns on Stribling. Much will be made of his speed and separation skills, which is fair. But he’s a bigger body who is unafraid to go over the middle. With Jauan Jennings gone, adding someone who brings that size and fearlessness (with plus speed, to boot) could help open things up for Purdy and Co.” The safety position has one constant through two days Day one of camp featured Ji’Ayir Brown and Marques Sigle to start the day, with Malik Mustapha rotating with Sigle. On day two, Brown was in the same spot with Mustapha starting and Sigle rotating with Mustapha. It’s only two days, but so far, Brown has settled into one spot with the other two 49ers draft picks auditioning for the spot opposite him. Perhaps Raheem Morris wants two free safety types, which would be Brown and Sigle. Brown intercepted Purdy on an in-breaking route that was intended for Jacob Cowing. So far, Connor Colby (LG), Nick Martin (SAM LB), and Brown have been the frontrunners at each position. Let’s see how long that lasts. The five-man defensive front integration continues We wondered what wrinkles Morris would add to the 49ers defense, and through two sessions, the 49ers have been implementing five-man fronts into their defensive scheme. Trent Williams spoke about the new look after Sunday’s practice, and Purdy spoke about it after yesterday’s session. Wagoner believes this is here to stay. “The use of 5-man fronts is going to be a discussion that continues to pick up as the year goes on. It’s early, but the Niners seem to be doing more than just toying with it as a gimmick here and there. Purdy even acknowledged that things look quite a bit different going against Raheem Morris’ defense than what the Niners have done previously.” For a longer discussion about day two of 49ers training camp, check out the video below:

title: Vita Vea reportedly wants to play on the West Coast; do the 49ers have the pieces for a trade?
summary: The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen tweeted that Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea, who requested a trade on Tuesday, wants to go to a California team or the Las Vegas Raiders. Vea, 31, enters the final year of his four-year, $71 million contract signed in January 2022. Vea has been an enforcer along the interior for the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - DECEMBER 21: Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea (50) during an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Carolina Panthers on December 21, 2025 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen tweeted that Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea, who requested a trade on Tuesday, wants to go to a California team or the Las Vegas Raiders. Vea, 31, enters the final year of his four-year, $71 million contract signed in January 2022. Vea has been an enforcer along the interior for the Bucs since he entered the league. His production slipped a bit last season. Vea played the 15th-most snaps at his position (17th-most at nose tackle since 2023), but was 46th in defensive stops and 29th in sacks. He still had double-digit tackles for loss numbers a year ago and was 21st in pressure rate. Durability has also been a feather in Vea’s cap. He didn’t miss a game in 2025. Vea has only missed six games since he signed his contract extension in 2022. Going by the average annual salary for interior defensive linemen, Vea is the 19th-highest-paid player at his position — hence why he wants a new deal. We’ve seen these contract standoffs in early training camp often. More often than not, they end with some type of pay raise for the player. In Vea’s case, that could be adding incentives or guaranteed money this season without extending him. But that won’t prevent the Bucs from getting calls about Vea. If the situation reaches a point where there’s no coming back from, let’s look at what a potential trade for Vea would look like What a potential Vea trade would look like The Giants recently traded Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals. Lawrence, 28, went for the 10th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Lawrence is a different animal snaps-wise. No player has played more snaps than Lawrence at nose since 2023. While his volume is higher, Vea still has a better pressure rate. But Lawrence had two years remaining on his current deal. The other defensive tackle trade we can go off is Osa Odighizuwa. But this is far from an apples-to-apples trade. They play different positions. Odighizuwa is 3.5 years younger and is under contract through the 2028 season. It’s still puzzling to look back and see the Niners only needing to give up a third-rounder for Odighizuwa. Given Vea only having one year remaining on his contract, barring an overpay, his valuation is close to a mid- to late third-round pick. That includes age, production, positional value, and contract. Again, a team could swoop in and overpay, potentially offering a second-rounder, but that would be a surprising offer. As for the potential teams, the Rams have another defensive tackle they are trying to work things out with. We know how important stopping the run is in the eyes of Jim Harbaugh. The Chargers drafted a defensive tackle in the sixth round and signed veteran Dalvin Tomlinson. Those moves wouldn’t prevent them from acquiring Vea. The Raiders would be the team to offer over market value, as Vea would be a significant upgrade from what’s on the roster, outside of Maxx Crosby. The Niners are in win-now mode and have the cap space to make the deal happen. Vea’s owed $17 million in 2026. Vea, who grew up in the Bay Area and attended Milpitas High School, would be one of the few veterans on a team that is a year removed from making a youth movement at defensive tackle. You probably don’t want to include Alfred Collins in a hypothetical trade. However, maybe C.J. West and a third-rounder would do the trick. You could mix and match younger players to entice a deal, but the Bucs would likely want a draft pick back as well. What do you think it would take for the 49ers to acquire Vea? Scroll down and let us know in the comments.

title: Brock Purdy explains why 49ers rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling is a ‘baller’
summary: So far, so good for San Francisco 49ers rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling. We’re reading about Stribling impressing early in training camp, making big plays downfield or creating yards after the catch by turning underneath routes into 20+ yard receptions. Stribling is performing like the player he was drafted to be. Brock Purdy is noticing […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - MAY 28: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on May 28, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images So far, so good for San Francisco 49ers rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling. We’re reading about Stribling impressing early in training camp, making big plays downfield or creating yards after the catch by turning underneath routes into 20+ yard receptions. Stribling is performing like the player he was drafted to be. Brock Purdy is noticing the rookie. On Monday, Purdy said, “Dude is a baller, and I mean that. It’s hard to say that for a rookie, right off the jump, but just seeing him run routes, going up against defenders in OTAs and then in camp yesterday. He’s a great route runner. He’s smart. He’s learned the playbook really quick, which is awesome. And then, on top of that, you can see his strength, too. When he’s going up against guys and creating separation, I’m like, ‘Alright, this guy’s a strong receiver.’ And so, I’m excited to see what he does, but all of us, all the quarterbacks in the room, were like, ‘Alright, this guy’s going to be the guy that’s going to come in and play.'” Stribling returned the compliments to Purdy, calling him a “Very talented guy, very talented guy, great leader.” Stribling continued: Just being out there with him, how he conducts the whole offense, keeps everyone in check, gives everyone their assignment. So, just trying to be there for him as a great receiver, reliable for him, and just doing my part.“ During his appearance on KNBR , Stribling was asked about the backlash the 49ers got for selecting him relatively early, compared to where the media had him. Stribling doesn’t concern himself with the media: It’s just media talk and media opinions. But at the end of the day, I felt like I played football at a high level. I did a lot of things all around, so I just let my film talk for itself. I don’t get too involved with all of that. At the end of the day, I have to go out there and catch the ball and score touchdowns and block. So, none of that matters until I’m out on the field. I’d expect Stribling to be used early and often, especially if George Kittle isn’t ready to play early in the season. It’s far from a 1-for-1 substitution, but Stribling has the aggressiveness and body type to block bigger bodies closer to the line of scrimmage — something the 49ers wideouts struggled with a season ago. And then you have the 10” hands that’ll make the margin for error greater for the 49ers quarterbacks, both from an accuracy perspective as well as when it comes to contested catch situations. Last season, Jauan Jennings only caught 46% of his contested catches. Stribling will look to improve on that number while playing a similar role.

title: The majority of 49ers fans believe John Lynch’s job should be safe if the team misses the playoffs
summary: In our weekly FanDuel Sportsbook survey, we asked San Francisco 49ers fans whether the team should part ways with John Lynch if the team misses the playoffs in 2026. The 49ers would likely need to suffer multiple injuries at critical positions once again to miss the playoffs. Depending on where you look, the Niners are […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 24: John Lynch of the San Francisco 49ers speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images In our weekly FanDuel Sportsbook survey, we asked San Francisco 49ers fans whether the team should part ways with John Lynch if the team misses the playoffs in 2026. The 49ers would likely need to suffer multiple injuries at critical positions once again to miss the playoffs. Depending on where you look, the Niners are projected to finish anywhere between the top three and the top five teams in the NFC. The expectation is for them to make the postseason. Even if there were injuries, disappointments, or shortcomings of some sort, 49ers fans are still willing to give general manager John Lynch grace if the team doesn’t make the playoffs in 2026. That makes it seem like the question was silly and should’ve never been posed. The 49ers have been one of the most successful franchises this decade. They’ve made the playoffs multiple times, including appearances in the NFC Championship and Super Bowl. For as much flak as the organization has received for some of their top draft picks not panning out, not enough credit has been given for the team’s willingness to move on when they’ve realized they’ve made a mistake. You also can’t help but applaud their aggressiveness. From trading up or down in the draft, moving draft picks for established veterans, or taking swings in free agency, John Lynch and the 49ers front office have put this team in a position to compete at a high level.

title: What role will Titans WR Elic Ayomanor play in 2026?
summary: The Tennessee Titans have their first training camp practice on Wednesday. One of the big storylines is the new-look wide receiver room. Sophomore Elic Ayomanor is tasked with navigating how he fits in Brian Daboll’s offense. The Titans signed Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70 million contract in free agency. Mike Borgonzi doubled down on […]
full_text: Jun 16, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans wide receiver Elic Ayomanor (5) makes a catch during day 1 of mini-camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans have their first training camp practice on Wednesday. One of the big storylines is the new-look wide receiver room. Sophomore Elic Ayomanor is tasked with navigating how he fits in Brian Daboll’s offense. The Titans signed Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70 million contract in free agency. Mike Borgonzi doubled down on Cam Ward’s development by drafting Carnell Tate with the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Like Chimere Dike, Ayomanor is a sophomore trying to navigate all the newness. Last season, the Titans were overly reliant on Ayomanor, the third of three fourth-round picks they made in 2025. Ayomanor finished second on the Titans in receiving yards (515) and tied for first in touchdowns (4, with fellow rookie Dike). The former Stanford standout placed fifth in receptions with 41. Ayomanor and Dike unexpectedly ended up in starring roles. Calvin Ridley suffered a season-ending injury during the first half of the campaign. Veteran Tyler Lockett was released after proving to be ineffective. Ayomanor and Dike were asked to pick up the slack. By adding Robinson and Tate, and retaining Ridley, the Titans are far better prepared at receiver. The assumption is that Tate will be the starting X receiver. Robinson is a slot, and both Ridley and Dike can play the Z position. Ayomanor is a throwback X receiver. He’s obviously not going to beat-out Tate for that role. The Titans could move personnel around, with Tate, Robinson, and Dike all being flexible enough to play different positions. Ayomanor could find himself at X in certain packages. Ayomanor was a useful receiver as a rookie throughout the 2025 season. The Titans desperately needed to get better at the pass-catching spots though, and that’s precisely what they did this offseason, to better support Ward. Ayomanor must navigate those challenges and compete for reps.

title: Mike Borgonzi keeps relying on familiarity to bolster Titans’ CB depth
summary: Tennessee Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi totally revamped the cornerback room this offseason. It was necessary after he gutted the position by trading Jarvis Brownlee and Roger McCreary, and cut L’Jarius Sneed. As soon as free agency began, Borgonzi signed Alontae Taylor, Cor’Dale Flott, and Joshua Williams to be the Titans’ top three new boundary […]
full_text: Photo of the new Titans helmets set up during a pre NFL draft press conference held at the Titans practice facility Thursday, April 16, 2026. | Alan Poizner/For The Tennessean / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Tennessee Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi totally revamped the cornerback room this offseason . It was necessary after he gutted the position by trading Jarvis Brownlee and Roger McCreary, and cut L’Jarius Sneed. As soon as free agency began, Borgonzi signed Alontae Taylor, Cor’Dale Flott, and Joshua Williams to be the Titans’ top three new boundary corners. Now, a fourth addition has arrived. The Titans agreed to terms with cornerback Nazeeh Johnson before training camp opened. Johnson marks the second former Kansas City Chiefs cornerback to sign with the Titans this offseason, joining Williams. It seems that Borgonzi is very content to rely on familiarity to remake the Titans’ depth at cornerback. He didn’t know Flott and Taylor from Kansas City, but still signed them to very lucrative contracts to be the new starters. But when it came to supporting Flott and Taylor, he felt comfortable calling on Williams, and now Johnson. Borgonzi was with the Chiefs when they drafted both Williams and Johnson. That certainly isn’t a coincidence. He’s also signed defensive end Malik Herring and punter Tommy Townsend this offseason, two other players he spent time with in KC. Essentially every free agent the Titans signed this offseason had ties to Borgonzi or the new coaching staff. Daniel Bellinger, Flott, Austin Schlottmann, and Wan’Dale Robinson have connections to Brian Daboll. John Franklin-Myers, Jacob Martin, Solomon Thomas, Tony Adams, and Jordan Elliott are among those with connections to Robert Saleh. Williams is essentially guaranteed to be the Titans’ primary backup cornerback on the outside behind Flott and Taylor. Johnson probably isn’t assured a 53-man roster spot, but he has a decent chance to compete for the fifth cornerback role with Micah Robinson, Keydrain Calligan, and a bunch of undrafted free agent rookies. Johnson will arrive at training camp with designs on making the 53-man roster.

title: Commanders: Five things we learned from Dan Quinn, Adam Peters presser
summary: Commanders training camp is underway. The full squad is checked in. The staff is ready for heightened activity and the coaches believe they’ve set up a plan for success and development over the next several weeks as preparation for the 2026 season begins in earnest.   The vibes are high around the Commanders training complex […]
full_text: Commanders training camp is underway. The full squad is checked in. The staff is ready for heightened activity and the coaches believe they’ve set up a plan for success and development over the next several weeks as preparation for the 2026 season begins in earnest. The vibes are high around the Commanders training complex in Ashburn, VA, something that was clear at the start of Tuesday evening’s press conference with head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters. “I’m excited for you guys to feel the energy of the team, their readiness, their swagger,” Quinn said. “As we get started, I’m excited for you all to feel that.” Peters backed that up with this: “I’m excited as I’ve ever been. There’s a ton of great energy from all aspects of the building, to see how this is going to unfold.” There’s belief in a quick rebound from last season’s mess, with new coordinators, quarterback Jayden Daniels’ rejuvenated health, and a bunch of free agents and draft picks ready to join the fight. Here are five things we learned from Tuesday’s remarks: Commanders are happy at WR, but… Peters added to his receiver group on several occasions, most notably with the third-round Antonio Williams draft pick and Dyami Brown’s return in free agency. There are several (including me) wondering if they need to add another veteran receiver to the mix. The GM was asked about adding another talent to the roster, and had this to say: “I’m happy with what we’ve done throughout the offseason. Our staff did a great job identifying guys who would help us, both offensively and defensively,” Peters said. “Specifically, wide receiver-wise, we’re really happy with who’s in that room and how the guys progressed in the offseason and stepped up and will take another step in this training camp. “Like any other room in any other place, if we have ways to get better we’re always going to look into that and really assess the decision and whether it’s the right move for our team or not. If it is, we’re not afraid to do that.” So, yeah, the door’s still open. DMV native Stefon Diggs seems like a decent option . Brandon Aiyuk did a while ago, but his often off-putting social media antics have seemingly made him a far less attractive option should the 49ers receiver ever apply for reinstatement off the reserve/left-squad list and be released by San Francisco. NBC4’s JP Finlay , in an expertly phrased question that got a laugh from Peters and Quinn, asked if social media can impact an evaluation. “We do look at everything,” Peters said. “We want to make sure it’s the right player to be in our locker room and our bloodstream and our culture. We look at that stuff. It’s not always the first thing we look at. You look at the tape and you look at the teams the players have been on and how they were in the locker room with the players they were playing with to make those decisions. But, yeah, that’s not usually a huge part of it. Usually.” It’s worth watching this exchange in full: This was a fun moment but I do appreciate AP giving a real answer pic.twitter.com/tGV9zVMR46 — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) July 28, 2026 There’s belief in the CB corps…full stop The Commanders signed veteran cornerback Rasul Douglas earlier this month, but it wasn’t to fill a void. Peters didn’t see a deficiency in the group, only the possibility to add depth and experience to a premium position. He made that clear on Tuesday when asked about the Douglas addition. “He started a lot of games recently, and he always performs,” Peters said. “So, when you have an opportunity to add to that room, it’s not a deficiency in the room at all. You just want to make each room as strong as it can be. So, getting him in, we’re really excited about that. And we just got a chance to meet him yesterday. He’s big, and he’s played a lot of good ball. We’re excited to have him.” It’s clear the Commanders are confident in the cornerback room overall — Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson were singled out as team leaders — with optimism that those players will fit well within Daronte Jones’ scheme. “It’s actually a deep group, we feel, going into it,” Quinn said. “And so, I think kind of the secret sauce is, how do we fit in? Well, who’s going to play inside? Who’s going to play outside? How can we work through that? And I think that, in itself, is going to be some intrigue, and it’ll take a few weeks for us to get to that space.” Jayden Daniels’ ‘hunger’ Daniels is coming off a 2025 season where he missed 10 games and finished just four. That rough follow-up to an NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign is in his rearview – he made that clear during the offseason program — and he’s ready to meld with David Blough’s new offense and return to regularly fine form. That has been clear during the spring and into this summer’s camp. “You felt his hunger from the beginning this offseason, with the way he went after it,” Quinn said. “Just his ability to understand this scheme that quickly, it’s not easy for anyone to do. He often makes the difficult things look easy, but … he absolutely has that.” Commanders have big plans for Chig It sure seems like the Commanders have big plans for new tight end Chig Okonkwo . The free-agent signing from Tennessee does a lot of things well, especially in the passing game. That’s prized in the scheme we expect David Blough to run. That was clear hearing Peters talk about him on Tuesday evening, that Okonkwo’s presence will allow the Commanders to do some creative things. “He’s an outstanding receiver. He’s outstanding in the pass game,” Peters said. “He’s great after the catch, you know, and he’s also a really good blocker . A good competitive blocker. He’s not the biggest tight end. He’s not [TE] John Bates, but we really love the way he competes as a blocker and how he executes there too.” “He’s got a really good skill set, but he does help us quite a bit in the pass game. So, he allows you to be a little bit more multiple. You know, you can go more two tight end sets; you can go one tight end set. It’s like you almost have four receivers on the field. He provides a lot of versatility in where he can line up and what he can do for us when he gets the ball in his hands. And then he’s pretty magical.” Quinn confident in Nick Allegretti Nick Allegretti seems set to play center for the Commanders this season despite most of his NFL experience coming at guard. There’s no trepidation handing Allegretti such a plum assignment with tons of pre-snap responsibility. After hearing comments from Quinn, it was clear Washington was comfortable letting Tyler Biadasz walk . “We’ve got a lot of faith and confidence in him,” Quinn said. “It’s another one of the positions that we do have competition that we’re going for. But, if Nick was playing on defense, he’d be a green dot. This is one of the smartest guys on our team now. Like, we talk about putting it under control, that’s part of playing center. And he has that targeting. ‘Who’s this? Where’s the protection going?’ We’ve got a lot of confidence in him. He is one hell of a competitor. And so, he’s one of those guys, man, you don’t bet against that.”

summary: Wes Welker will be coaching the Commanders tight ends “moving forward,” head coach Dan Quinn announced in a Tuesday press conference. full_text: Wes Welker will be coaching the Commanders tight ends “moving forward,” head coach Dan Quinn announced in a Tuesday press conference . While he didn’t formally refer to Welker, an offensive assistant, with the title of tight ends coach, Quinn said that Welker will take over coaching the position group. A change was necessary after the team dismissed Ben Steele on Monday. Per The Athletic’s Nick Jhabvala , Steele was let go for violating team policy. The change came more than a month after Steele was arrested on suspicion. of DWI. Per Virginia court records , Steele has since been charged with DWI, refusal to submit to a field blood/breath test, obstruction/resisting arrest without force and changing course without a signal. Steele was new to the Commanders , hired earlier in 2026. Welker coached the Commanders tight ends during mandatory minicamp last month, while Steele was on leave. A permanent replacement was required after Steele was let go, and Welker was given the assignment David Raih was promoted to passing game coordinator this offseason after two seasons coaching the tight ends, but he’ll remain in his current position. Stay tuned for more on this developing story.

title: Commanders training camp primer: Key dates, position battles, storylines
summary: Commanders training camp is (finally) upon us.  Rookies, quarterbacks and some rehabbing players have been in Ashburn, VA a few days now, but the full squad reports Tuesday.   The first practice of training camp is Wednesday, and then we’re off. Washington will conduct two joint practices, play three preseason games and conduct dozens of […]
full_text: Commanders training camp is (finally) upon us. Rookies, quarterbacks and some rehabbing players have been in Ashburn, VA a few days now, but the full squad reports Tuesday. The first practice of training camp is Wednesday, and then we’re off. Washington will conduct two joint practices , play three preseason games and conduct dozens of practices either in shells or pads or in a walk-through format. Head coach Dan Quinn, general manager Adam Peters, and their staffs will use those touch points to bring their 91-man roster down to the 53 they’ll take into the first game of a pivotal regular season. We’ve got miles to go before we reach that point, with competition creating separation and arranging the depth chart. A QUICK READER SURVEY With training camp now upon us, let’s get a bird’s-eye view of what’s to come for the Commanders: Training camp dates Location: Bigbear.ai Performance Center (Ashburn, VA) Dates: July 29, 30, Aug. 1*, 3*, 4*, 5*, 7*, 8*, 10*, 11*, 12*, 18*, 19*, 20, 25 * Practices open to fans ( all dates sold out except Aug. 11-12 , and those are only open to season-ticket members ) Joint practices: Aug. 12: vs. Miami in Ashburn; Aug. 26: @ Baltimore 53-man roster cut: Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET Preseason games Week 1 – vs Miami Dolphins (Friday, August 14, 6 p.m. ET, CBS) Week 2 – @ Detroit Lions (Saturday, August 22, 12 p.m.; CBS) Week 3 – @ Baltimore Ravens (Friday, August 28, 7 p.m., CBS) Camp battles RB: Bill Croskey-Merritt vs. Rachaad White | LG: Chris Paul vs. Brandon Coleman | WR: Luke McCaffrey vs. Jaylin Lane | WR: Treylon Burks vs. Antonio Williams | C : Nick Allegretti vs. Matt Gulbin | K: Jake Moody vs. Drew Stevens | RB: Jerome Ford vs. Jeremy McNichols | CB: Rasul Douglas vs. Mike Sainristil Camp storylines Keep an eye on David Blough, Daronte Jones The Commanders will run new schematics in 2026 on both sides of the ball. David Blough is installing a new offense based on under-center snaps, zone rushing concepts and playaction. Daronte Jones will create a multiple, attacking defense. Both guys are first-time NFL play callers – Jones was LSU’s DC for one season – so they must teach new systems well. Then they’ll refine them based on the talent available. And, eventually, they must game plan and call the right plays at the right time. Optimism is high that Blough and Jones will bring new life into Commanders football , but bumpy roads should be expected in training camp. Mistakes will be made; pre-snap work might start slow, but that’s why we have training camp and the preseason. The Commanders are banking on these two fresh faces to come through. It’s up to Blough and Jones to validate these bold hires. Stefon Diggs on the way? So much offseason talk was spent on the Commanders possibly adding a WR2 to the lineup. Much of it was focused on Brandon Aiyuk, but his social-media antics may have put an end to that (keywords: may have). DMV native Stefon Diggs is still available – he’s got some off-field baggage of his own – but would provide an instant upgrade to the receiver corps. Washington has the money to sign Diggs, and may need to overpay a bit to secure him. Will they do so, or stand pat with the collection of talent already assembled? Time will tell (quickl) on that front, though an early injury or position group struggles may force Peters’ hand. Opportunity ahead for NFL Draft class It’s never good to need a rookie to play a massive role, especially outside the first-round picks. No. 7 overall selection Sonny Styles should be a three-down linebacker, but the Commanders could sure use third-round receiver Antonio Williams to play a prominent role in the passing game . Washington would also benefit from sixth-round running back Kaytron Allen as an immediate short-yardage option. Of course, they’re also counting on undrafted kicker Drew Stevens to put pressure on incumbent Jake Moody. Those aren’t desires. Those are needs. That’s scary, because you can’t assume rookies will be ready. As camp progresses, keep close tabs on those four in particular , for signs that they’ll be ready to contribute at some point in the early regular season.

full_text: The Daily Slop – 28 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Pro Football Focus PFF Tight End Rankings: The top 32 players ahead of the 2026 NFL season 25. Chigoziem Okonkwo , Washington Commanders After four seasons with the Titans, Okonkwo joined the Commanders on a three-year, $27 million contract. He’s most dangerous with the ball in his hands: Last year, Okonkwo’s 13 forced missed tackles were fourth in the NFL, while his 345 yards after the catch were ninth. It is worth mentioning though that he did post the lowest PFF run-blocking grade of any tight end in the NFL in 2025 (27.9). To read more of this article, CLICK HERE NFL.com NFL MVP: One non-QB candidate from each NFC team in 2026 As we sit here today, McLaurin isn’t just the Commanders’ top target — he’s the only receiver on the club who had more than 400 yards last season. Washington could still add a veteran — Stefon Diggs or Brandon Aiyuk ( if he’s ever released and if he still wants to play football) — but as we enter training camp, it’s all Scary Terry. He’s coming off an injury-plagued season in which he played just 10 games, recording career lows in catches (38), yards (582) and touchdowns (three). McLaurin and Jayden Daniels participated in just three games together all season. If both stay healthy, expect McLaurin’s production to skyrocket back to where it was when the wideout earned second-team All-Pro honors while catching 13 TDs in 2024. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com One Commanders player to watch at every position group in training camp Defensive end Charles Omenihu: Omenihu is not considered one of the top defensive ends in the NFL, but he’s a smart player with seven years of experience that he can offer the position. He’s going to be a depth piece for the group who could have some impactful plays because of his length and power. Outside linebacker Odafe Oweh: Oweh is at the forefront of the Commanders’ efforts to rejuvenate their pass rush in 2026. He’s coming off a season in which he had 10 combined sacks in the regular and postseason, and the Commanders believe he’s on the cusp of being one of the better pass rushers in the NFL with his athleticism and speed. He’ll be a fun piece for defensive coordinator Daronte Jones to move around to rush passers. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A QUICK READER SURVEY A to Z Sports Commanders’ explosive UDFA WR leads pack of 3 underdog rookies [Jaden] Bradley is a 6-foot-4, 195-pound pass catcher who signed a three-year, $3.1 million contract with Washington that includes $55,000 guaranteed. Now, these kinds of contracts aren’t necessarily an indicator a player will make the team. However, it does show the organization has a lot of faith in him. And, he has the exact size most of his counterparts lack. With so much fluidity behind McLaurin, anything is possible for Bradley, who finished with 86 receptions for 1,363 yards and seven touchdowns over the course of his college career. He easily had the best year of his career in 2025 with UNLV, catching 58 passes for 931 yards and four touchdowns. That comes out to a 16.1-yard average per reception, and it’s easy to see why Bradley can quickly make a name for himself. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Nick Bellore’s retirement changes Commanders’ roster math before training camp Bellore played 338 total snaps on special teams, which accounts for 79% of Washington’s total special teams plays in 2025. Jordan Magee, Kain Medrano, and Ale Kaho…are all ready to take a larger role with the team. Medrano and Kaho, in particular, stand to benefit from having one fewer linebacker competing for a roster spot and a significant special-teams role now available . Bellore’s 338 snaps will likely be evenly distributed among those who make the final 53-man roster. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Wire Four biggest position battles heading into Commanders training camp Right now, it seems like Douglas, Mike Sainristil, and Ahkello Witherspoon are fighting for the starting corner spot opposite Trey Amos. However, Amos was recently put on the PUP list, so it will be interesting to see if that affects the competition. If Amos has to miss time, the team will probably turn to Douglas and Sainristil as the two boundary corners. There’s also a battle for the final spot. Assume Amos, Sainristil, Douglas, and Amik Robertson are locks, that could leave just one spot for Witherspoon, Antonio Hamilton Sr., and Darius Rush, among others. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Nick Allegretti can alleviate Commanders fans’ concerns at training camp ESPN insider John Keim believes that a strong camp from Allegretti will alleviate some concerns fans have about the move. The Commanders are reportedly encouraged by his leadership and high football IQ. This is also where he feels comfortable, so all signs point upward before things get more intense. “The coaches say there’s a competition for this position, but Allegretti has, by far, the most experience with 39 starts — but only four at center. He calls it his natural position, however, and the Commanders do like his smarts and leadership skills. A strong showing in camp will answer a key question for Washington.” Allegretti is being pushed by sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin, but the winner of this position battle should be a formality. It’s the veteran’s job to lose, but the hard work is only just beginning. The Commanders placed a lot of faith in Allegretti. Cutting Biadasz and giving the Super Bowl winner a contract extension were major calls by general manager Adam Peters. His production at either guard position doesn’t exactly bode well, but if he is more comfortable at center, all hope is not lost just yet. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Details emerge after Commanders part ways with TE coach Ben Steele According to Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic , Steele was arrested on suspicion of driving while intoxicated on June 7. He also faces additional charges for refusing blood and breath tests, in addition to obstructing or resisting an officer without force. Steele has not been part of the Commanders’ setup since minicamp, as he was placed on leave after informing the franchise of his arrest. Wes Welker coached the tight end unit in his absence, and he has now been let go for violating team policy. Jhabvala also revealed that head coach Dan Quinn is expected to announce his replacement on Tuesday , on the eve of Washington’s first training camp practice in Ashburn. There was significant intrigue around Steele’s arrival in Washington. He spent three productive seasons with the Arizona Cardinals, where he was instrumental in turning Trey McBride into an elite-level pass-catcher at the position. With free-agent signing Chig Okonkwo , John Bates, and 2024 second-round pick Ben Sinnott, he also had a decent amount to work with on the Commanders. Now, that won’t happen. The Commanders run a tight ship, and issues like this are not looked upon favorably by those in power. Steele found that out to his cost, and an extremely uncertain future now awaits. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is expected to announce Steele’s replacement Tuesday. This likely means the team will either go with Wes Welker, who handled the tight ends during minicamp, or call on David Raih to assume that role again. Raih was the tight ends coach for the Commanders the last two seasons and was promoted…
